2150 Time Synchronisation and Future Dated Remote Party Messages
2151 This Section 9 details how time synchronisation shall operate, and how future dated Remote
2152 Party Messages shall be processed by Devices. The latter applies only where a Command is
2153 specified in ‘Use Case reference’ tab in the Mapping Table, as ‘Capable of future dated
2154 invocation’.
Page 119

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
2155 Note that all references in the GBCS to time shall be to UTC date-time unless explicitly stated
2156 otherwise.
2157 Time synchronisation
2158 Introduction – informative
2159 SMETS requires that SAPC, ESME and GSME have clocks and that, under normal operating
2160 circumstances, the time on those clocks is accurate to within 10 seconds.
2161 CHTS requires that Communications Hubs have clocks and that, under normal operating
2162 circumstances, the time on those clocks is accurate to within 10 seconds.
2163 Critical functionality on Communications Hubs can function predictably without reliance on
2164 time. Time setting mechanisms on Communications Hubs therefore are not constrained or
2165 specified in the GBCS. However, under normal operating circumstances, a Communications
2166 Hub will provide the time reference for all dependent Devices on the HAN.
2167 Significant parts of SAPC, ESME and GSME functionality are time-dependent for their correct
2168 and predictable functioning. This includes Critical functionality which can only be controlled
2169 by the Device’s Supplier with responsibility for that Device. Thus, time must be accurate in
2170 terms of alignment with the time set by the Supplier on the Device. However, the accuracy
2171 requirements measured in seconds are smaller than end-to-end network latency for delivery
2172 of Commands to Devices.
2173 This leads to a time synchronisation approach for ESME and SAPC as specified in Section
2174 9.1.4, and GSME as specified in Section 9.1.7.
2175 That approach is:
2176 for the Supplier to send a Set Clock Command with the Supplier’s current time and a future
2177 time (reflecting a time tolerance) in the Command; and
2178 if, when the Device receives the Command, the Communications Hub’s time is within
2179 tolerance of the Supplier’s time, the Device aligns itself to the Communications Hub’s time
2180 and treats its time as Reliable. Otherwise the Device treats its time as Unreliable.
2181 The time synchronisation for a GSME follows the same principles but tolerance needs to
2182 differ because a GSME is ‘sleepy’. ‘Sleepy’ means that its SMHAN radio will not be active
2183 most of the time and therefore the tolerance provided by the Supplier needs to reflect the
2184 extended latency.
2185 Common Requirements – Set Clock
2186 Supplier Current Time shall be the Supplier’s time at the point the Supplier sends a Set Clock
2187 Command.
Page 120

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
2188 GSME and ESME shall maintain a record of its Time Status, which, for clarity, is not the same
2189 as the ZSE TimeStatus attribute in the Remote Communications Endpoint. Time Status shall
2190 have one of the values in Table 9.1.2.
Page 121

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
Value Meaning
Invalid The Device has no meaningful time
Unreliable The Device has a meaningful time but that time may not be accurate and
needs to be affirmed / reaffirmed by the Supplier
Reliable The Device has a meaningful time and that time has been affirmed by its
Supplier
2191 Table 9.1.2: Time Status
2192 Device Requirements relating to the ZCL Time Cluster and its usage
2193 Requirements in this Section 9.1.3 shall apply to an SAPC as if it were an ESME.
2194 All italicised terms in this Section 9.1.3 shall have the meanings defined in the Time Cluster
2195 specification within the ZigBee Cluster Library Specification.
2196 In relation to the ZCL Time Cluster in the Remote Communications Endpoint, a
2197 Communications Hub shall:
2198 set the Time attribute to the UTCTime provided to it via its WAN interface, whenever such
2199 time information is available to it via its WAN interface and maintain its internal clock to the
2200 tolerance required by the CHTS;
2201 set the Time attribute to 0xFFFFFFFF whenever it cannot maintain its time via its WAN
2202 interface to the tolerance required by the CHTS due to resetting its internal clock;
2203 whenever its Time attribute has the value 0xFFFFFFFF, store the value 0xFFFFFFFF in any
2204 unsigned 32 bit integer format time stamps it records and store the value
2205 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF8000FF in any DLMS COSEM octet-string(12) format time stamps it
2206 records; and
2207 always have TimeStatus attributes set as:
2208 Attribute Bit Number 0 (Master) equal to 0b1 (master clock);
2209 Attribute Bit Number 2 (MasterZoneDst) equal to 0b0 (not master for Time Zone and DST);
2210 and
2211 Attribute Bit Number 3 (Superseding) equal to 0b1 (time synchronisation can supersede).
2212 In relation to any ZigBee Time Cluster on the ESME, the ESME shall always have TimeStatus
2213 attributes set as:
2214 Attribute Bit Number 0 (Master) equal to 0b0 (not master clock); and
Page 122

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
2215 Attribute Bit Number 3 (Superseding) equal to 0b0 (time synchronisation should not be
2216 superseded).
2217 At power on of the clock, an ESME or GSME shall:
2218 set its Time Status as ‘Invalid’;
2219 attempt to synchronise time, using the Communications Hub’s Time Cluster; and
2220 where a valid Time (so not 0xFFFFFFFF) is provided by the Communications Hub before any
2221 Set Clock Command is received, set its time to the value of Time provided and set its Time
2222 Status to ‘Unreliable’.
2223 ESME and GSME shall attempt to synchronise time, using the Communications Hub’s Remote
2224 Communications Endpoint Time Cluster, once every 24 hour period in line with the SMETS
2225 requirement. ESME and GSME shall undertake the following processing dependent on the
2226 outcome of each attempted synchronisation:
2227 if a time of 0xFFFFFFFF is provided or if no time is received the Device shall retry the
2228 synchronisation after an elapsed period of 30 minutes, for a minimum of the lesser of three
2229 retries, or a retry resulting in a valid Time (so not 0xFFFFFFFF) being provided. If no valid
2230 Time has been provided after three retries, the Device shall set its Time Status to
2231 ‘Unreliable’;
2232 if the time provided by the Communications Hub differs from the Device’s time by more
2233 than 10 seconds, then the Device shall:
2234 set its Time Status to ‘Unreliable’; and
2235 if this results in a change to Time Status, the Device shall construct and issue an Alert with
2236 Alert Code 0x8F0C, meaning that its time would have been shifted by more than 10 seconds.
2237 If the Device is a GSME, the Alert Payload shall be a GBZ Alert Payload. If the Device is an
2238 ESME, the Alert Payload shall be a DLMS COSEM Alert Payload.
2239 if the time provided by the Communications Hub differs from the Device’s time by 10
2240 seconds or less, then the Device shall adjust its time to the Communications Hub’s time.

2243 an SAPC as if it were an ESME.
2244 This Use Case covers the setting of the Clock by the Supplier on an ESME.

2403  Future Dated Commands for the Reading of Data Items – informative
2404  Where future dated execution of a Command to read data items is supported in a Use Case,
2405  this is achieved by setting values in a schedule stored on the Device.  In such cases, the
| 2406  sequence of Messages is as follows:  |     |     |     |
| ------------------------------------------ | --- | --- | --- |
2407  on receipt of a Command to update a schedule, the Device should attempt to Authenticate
2408  then execute the Command.  The Device should then create a corresponding Response
2409  either indicating the schedule has been set or providing failure reasons; and
2410  when each trigger time in the schedule is reached (according to the Clock on the Device),
2411  the Device undertakes the required processing then creates and sends an Alert.  One initial
2412  Command to set a schedule may generate many such Alerts.
|     |     |     | Page 131  |
| --- | --- | --- | --------- |

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
2413 In such circumstances, the Command and Response are specified in one Use Case, and the
2414 Alert is specified in a different Use Case.
2415 Such future dated reading can be cancelled by sending a Command which resets the
2416 schedule values.
2417 The only example of such a schedule is the Billing Calendar. The Alerts generated are Billing
2418 Calendar Alerts.
2419 Future Dated Commands for the Writing of Attributes
2420 Introduction – informative
2421 Only Commands marked ‘Capable of future dated invocation?’ in the Mapping Table can be
2422 future dated. Such Commands allow a data item or group of data items to be changed at a
2423 date-time in the future.
2424 Where a data item or group of data items on a Device are capable of future dated updates,
2425 this is achieved by the Device having:
2426 a ‘current’ and a ‘next’ version of the group of data items in question;
2427 a data item for recording the date / time at which the ‘next’ version should be made
2428 ‘current’; and
2429 a method to set ‘current’ values equal to ‘next’ values.
2430 This is the meaning of data items with ‘Current’ and ‘Next’ post fixes in the ‘SMETS / CHTS
2431 Attribute / method’ column of the Mapping Table.
2432 In such cases, the sequence of Messages to effect a future dated update would be:
2433 1. a Command would be sent to the Device instructing that the data items in question
2434 should be stored in the ‘next’ data items and the corresponding activation date /
2435 time should be set (so overwriting previous ‘next’ values and any previous activation
2436 date / time);
2437 2. only if the Command is Authenticated, would the Device attempt to execute the
2438 instructions in Command. Execution for such Commands means writing to ‘next’
2439 values and setting activation date-times. If the activation date-times are in the past,
2440 the Device will also attempt to make the ‘next’ values ‘current’;
2441 3. the Device would then create a Response. This Response would either confirm that
2442 the ‘next’ values and the activation date / time values have been set (and so any
2443 previous future dated command with this Message Code has been over written), or
2444 would provide failure reasons. The ‘current’ values would be unaffected assuming
2445 the activation date / times are in the future; and
Page 132

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
2446 4. when an activation date / time is reached (according to the clock on the Device), the
2447 Device would attempt to make the corresponding ‘next’ values ‘current’. The Device
2448 would then send an Alert detailing success or failure.
2449 Like all other Commands, future dated Commands cannot be modified once accepted by the
2450 Device. However, the time activated processing can be stopped from happening by sending
2451 a new Command of the same Message Type. This is because the new Command over writes
2452 the values from the old Command.
2453 For example:
2454 a ‘cancellation’ can be effected by sending a new Command where the activation date / time
2455 in the new Command has a value that means ‘never’ to the Device; and
2456 a ‘modification’ can be effected by sending a new Command where the activation date-time
2457 and / or the ‘next’ values in the new Command are different than the old one.
2458 Commands that are marked ‘Capable of future dated invocation?’ in the Mapping Table can
2459 also be invoked immediately, as specified in Section 9.2.2.4.
2460 When there is a change of Supplier on a Device which is (1) after a future dated change is
2461 stored but (2) before it is activated, the processing at Section 13.3.5.10 will be undertaken at
2462 the point of update of Security Credentials. This ensures future dated commands from the
2463 old Supplier will not be actioned by the Device.
2464 Date-times in future datable commands
2465 Where a Command contains more than one activation date-time field, the values in all
2466 activation date-times in an instance of that Command shall be the same, except for ZSE
2467 Command Payloads where a field contains 0xFFFFFFFF or 0xFFFFFFFE, then all activation
2468 date-times shall be either 0xFFFFFFFF or 0xFFFFFFFE. Devices shall reject Commands not
2469 complying with this requirement. A future datable Command shall be future dated when it
2470 contains an activation date-time that is not one of the values in Section 9.2.2.4.
2471 Effect on prior Commands of the same Message Code
2472 On receipt of an Authenticated future datable Command, the Device shall overwrite all parts
2473 of any previously sent future dated Command of the same Message Code and, if the
2474 activation date-times for the instructions in the Command are in the past, the Device shall
2475 execute the instructions immediately.
2476 Using a future dated Command to write Attributes immediately
2477 Where a Command is marked ‘Capable of future dated invocation?’ in the Mapping Table,
2478 instructions within the Command shall be executed immediately after Authentication by the
2479 Device when:
Page 133

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
2480 for DLMS COSEM Commands Payloads, activation date-time(s) have the value
2481 0x0000000000000000008000FF;
2482 for ZSE Command Payloads, the activation date-time(s) have the value 0x00000000; and
2483 for ASN.1 Command Payloads, the activation date-time is not present.
2484 Cancellation of future dated Commands for the writing of Attributes
2485 Where a Command is marked ‘Capable of future dated invocation?’ in the Mapping Table,
2486 instructions within the Command shall never be executed by the Device when:
2487 for DLMS COSEM Commands Payloads, activation date-time(s) have the value
2488 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF8000FF;
2489 for ZSE Command Payloads, the activation date-time(s) have the value 0xFFFFFFFF for any
2490 ZSE command other than PublishCalendar, PublishSpecialDays, PublishBlockThresholds,
2491 PublishPriceMatrix;
2492 for ZSE Command Payloads, the activation date-time(s) have the value 0xFFFFFFFE for the
2493 ZSE command PublishCalendar, PublishSpecialDays, PublishBlockThresholds,
2494 PublishPriceMatrix; and
2495 for ASN.1 commands, the activation date-time has a value of 99991231235959Z.
2496 For clarity, sending such a Command has the effect of ‘cancelling’ any previously sent future
2497 datable Command of the same Message Code that the Device has not already executed.
2498 Reactions to Future Dated Commands
2499 Subject to Command Authenticity and Integrity Verification as detailed in Section 6, where a
2500 Command is future dated, at time the Command is received, the Device shall send a
2501 Response to the Command:
2502 where activation date-times are in the past or the instructions detail immediate execution as
2503 per Section 9.2.2.4, the Command shall be executed immediately:
2504 for a CS02b Update Security Credentials Command, the processing shall be as required by
2505 Section 13.3.4.3;
2506 for a CS02g Update Load Controller Security Credentials Command, the processing shall be
2507 as required by Section 13.10.3.4;
2508 for a CS06 Activate Firmware, the processing shall be as required by Section 11.5.2.2; and
2509 for all other Commands, the Response shall detail the outcome of the Command’s execution,
2510 and no Alert shall be generated;
Page 134

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
2511 where activation date-times are in the future, that Response shall detail the success or
2512 otherwise of storing the details in the Command; and
2513 if the activation date-times are in the future and the Command's details were successfully
2514 stored, the Device shall, at the time the future activation date-time is reached, process each
2515 of the instructions, which contain an activation date-time, as specified in the Command in
2516 the sequence specified in that Command and then generate an Alert with an Alert Payload,
2517 for each instruction, of the same type as the Payload type of the Command and an Alert
2518 Code of 0x8F66 for successful execution and 0x8F67 for failed execution. Thus:
2519 an ASN.1 Command Payload shall lead to an ASN.1 Alert Payload, which shall be as defined

2521 a DLMS COSEM Command Payload shall lead to DLMS COSEM Alert Payload(s), which shall

2551 ZSE Implementation
2552 Italicised terms in this Section 10 shall have their meaning in the ZCL / ZSE specifications.
2553 Introduction – informative
2554 This Section 10 sets out specific requirements relating to the implementation of ZSE in
2555 Devices:
2556 Tunnels: requirements relating to Devices’ support for the Tunneling Cluster. This includes
2557 specific differences between GSME, HHT, VWD and other Devices, related to their use of the
2558 Tunneling Cluster. Note that all Devices except Type 2 Devices without Virtual WAN
2559 capability shall support the Tunneling Cluster, since this is the mechanism by which Remote
2560 Party Messages (and HAN Only Messages between a PPMID and a GSME) are transported
2561 over the HAN;
2562 GSME and GPF interactions (including the Tapping Off Mechanism (TOM)): this includes
2563 requirements relating to the GPF maintaining a copy of GSME data items, where copies are
2564 not supported natively by ZSE mirroring;
2565 GPF structured data items: requirements relating to how structured data items on the GPF
2566 are updated by the GSME and resulting values on the GPF are calculated; and
2567 HHT interactions – requirements relating to HHT connection to the SMHAN, including
2568 specific Tunneling Cluster related requirements.
2569 VWD interactions – requirements relating to VWD connection to the SMHAN, including
2570 specific Tunneling Cluster related requirements.
2571 Tunnels
2572 Overview – informative
2573 All Remote Party Messages are carried across the SMHAN using the Tunneling Cluster’s
2574 TransferData command.
2575 Type 2 Devices without Virtual WAN capability such as IHDs are not required to send or
2576 receive Remote Party Messages and so are not required to support the Tunneling Cluster.
2577 Remote Party Messages to and from the GPF do not cross the SMHAN and so do not use the
2578 Tunneling Cluster.
2579 All other types of Device need to be able to send and receive Remote Party Commands over
2580 the SMHAN and so, as specified in Section 10.2.2, shall support the Tunneling Cluster.
2581 Section 10.2.2 lays out the associated requirements, across all Devices including those for
2582 the GSME, VWD and HHT.

2584 Additional GSME requirements are laid out in Sections 10.2.4 and 10.3.
2585 HHT interactions also have specific requirements due to their function. These specific

2591 Requirements for the Tunneling Cluster
2592 Remote Party Messages and SME.C.PPMID-GSME Messages shall be transported over the
2593 SMHAN using the Tunneling Cluster’s TransferData command. Except where a TransferData
2594 command is to or from a GSME, the value of the Data field’s payload in the TransferData
2595 command shall be the Remote Party Message or SME.C.PPMID-GSME Message. Where a
2596 TransferData command is to or from a GSME, the Data field’s payload of the TransferData
2597 command shall take the values specified in Section 10.2.4.
2598 Devices supporting the Tunneling Cluster as a Server shall have a
2599 MaximumIncomingTransferSize set to 1500 octets, in line with the ZSE default. All Devices
2600 supporting the Tunneling Cluster shall use this value in any RequestTunnelResponse
2601 command and any RequestTunnel command.
2602 Devices shall set the value of the ManufacturerCode field in any RequestTunnel command to
2603 0xFFFF (‘not used’).
2604 The ProtocolID used for Messages sent or received using the CHF of a Virtual WAN CH as a
2605 Tunneling Cluster Client and VWD as a Tunneling Cluster Server shall be 0. The CHF shall set
2606 the value of the ProtocolID field in the RequestTunnel command to 0 and the CHF and VWD
2607 shall associate the TunnelID in the RequestTunnelResponse command with ProtocolID 0.
2608 In all other cases, the ProtocolID used for Remote Party Messages shall be 6. Devices shall
2609 set the value of the ProtocolID field in any RequestTunnel command to 6 and the CHF and
2610 Devices shall associate the TunnelID in the RequestTunnelResponse command with
2611 ProtocolID 6.
2612 Devices shall set the value of the FlowControlSupport field in any RequestTunnel command
2613 to ‘False’.

2639 Where a Device is required to support the Tunneling Cluster as a client, the tunneling client
2640 Device shall:
2641 whenever it sends a TransferDataError command with a TransferDataStatus of 0x00 (‘No

2643 tunnelling server Device; and
2644 whenever it receives a TransferDataError command with a currently valid TunnelID and a
2645 TransferDataStatus of 0x00 (‘No such tunnel’) from a tunneling server Device, close any

2741 CHF requirements for ESME Transfer Data commands
2742 Requirements in this Section 10.2.2.3 shall apply to an SAPC as if it were an ESME.
2743 When a CHF is sending a Remote Party Message to an ESME in a TransferData command, the
2744 CHF shall:
2745 set the Disable Default Response sub-field of the Frame Control field in the ZCL Header of
2746 the TransferData command to 0b0;
2747 if it is the first time this Remote Party Message has been sent by the CHF, set a counter (the
2748 ‘Message Transmission Counter’) for this Remote Party Message to 1. Otherwise increase
2749 the Message Transmission Counter by 1; and
2750 not send any subsequent Remote Party Message to the ESME until either:
2751 it has received a Default Response with a Status Code of SUCCESS in relation to a
2752 TransferData command containing the current Remote Party Message; or
2753 it has sent an Alert with Code 0x8F84 (‘Failure to Deliver Remote Party Message to ESME’) in
2754 relation to the current Remote Party Message.
2755 If the CHF receives a Default Response with a Status Code of SUCCESS to the TransferData
2756 command for the current Remote Party Message, the CHF may now send subsequent
2757 Remote Party Messages to the ESME.
2758 If the CHF receives no Default Response after 10 seconds, or receives a Default Response
2759 with a Status Code other than SUCCESS, to the TransferData command for the current
2760 Remote Party Message, the CHF shall start the Flow Control Replay Timer from 0 seconds.
Page 144

2761 When the Flow Control Replay Timer reaches 30 seconds:
2762 if the Message Transmission Counter for the current Remote Party Message is less than 3,
2763 the CHF shall retry delivery of the current Remote Party Message, by sending it in a new
2764 TransferData command to the ESME; or
2765 if the Message Transmission Counter for the current Remote Party Message is 3, the CHF
2766 shall:
2767 discard the current Remote Party Message; and
2768 log the event in its Event Log and send an Alert with Alert Code 0x8F84 (‘Failure to Deliver
2769 Remote Party Message to ESME’) and Message Code 0x00D5, in relation to the current
2770 Remote Party Message.

2820 GSME Tunnel Management – informative
2821 Commands are sent from the Communications Hub via the tunnel to the GSME. Since the
2822 GSME is a ‘sleepy’ Device, a mechanism is needed for the GSME to request that Commands
2823 are sent to it by the CHF.
Page 147

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
2824 In common with the transport of all Remote Party or SME.C.PPMID-GSME Messages, the
2825 mechanism used is the TransferData command, but TransferData commands sent between a
2826 GSME and CHF need to distinguish between when:
2827 the GSME is sending a Message, so an Alert or a Response or a GBT Message containing part
2828 of an Alert / Response;
2829 the GSME is asking the CHF to send it a Command, or a GBT Message containing part of a
2830 Command; and
2831 the CHF is sending the GSME a Command, or a GBT Message containing part of a Command.
2832 To meet this need, the following Sections specify additional structure in the first part of the
2833 Data parameter of the TransferData commands sent between GSME and CHF. Specifically
2834 the sending Device shall:
2835 where a Message is being sent, set the Data parameter payload in a TransferData command
2836 to the concatenation:
2837 Tunnel Manager Header || Message
2838 where a Message is not being sent (so when the GSME is requesting that a Message is sent),
2839 set the Data parameter payload in a TransferData command to the value of Tunnel Manager
2840 Header.
2841 A mechanism is also required to notify the GSME that one or more Commands are available
2842 for retrieval from the CHF.
2843 The ZSE specification has a flag called Tunnel Message Pending in the Functional Flag
2844 Notification definition. This flag is used to notify a GSME that the CHF has a Message
2845 waiting to be transferred to the GSME. The flag is set on the first pending Command and is
2846 reset when all Messages have been transferred to the GSME. The flag is available through
2847 the ReadAttribute or MirrorAttributeResponse command. The requirements for setting this
2848 flag are specified in Section 10.3.4.
2849 The Tunnel Manager Header identifies three different kinds of TransferData command
2850 usage:
2851 GET (the value 0x01): this is used by the GSME to retrieve waiting Message from the CHF;
2852 GET-RESPONSE (the concatenation 0x02 || (Number of Messages remaining for retrieval
2853 after this Message) || (Message addressed to the GSME)): this is used by the CHF to send a
2854 Message to the GSME. It also indicates how many Messages have yet to be retrieved; and
2855 PUT(the value 0x03): this is used by the GSME to send a Message via the CHF.
Page 148

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
2856 Where a Command is waiting on the CHF for the GSME to retrieve it, the following sequence
2857 shall apply:
2858 1. the Tunnel Message Pending flag is set on the Communications Hub as detailed in
2859 Section 10.3.4;
2860 2. the GSME turns on its HAN Interface and obtains the value of the Tunnel Message
2861 Pending flag; and
2862 3. If the Tunnel Message Pending flag is set:
2863 1. the GSME sends a TransferData command to the CHF with the GET structure in the
2864 Tunnel Manager Header. The Tunnel Manager Header is the only content in the Data
2865 field of this TransferData command;
2866 the CHF sends a TransferData command to the GSME with the GET-RESPONSE structure in
2867 the Tunnel Manager Header and a Message in the remaining part of the Data field of the
2868 command. The GET-RESPONSE structure details how many more Messages are available for
2869 retrieval; and
2870 the GET and GET-RESPONSE pattern repeats until all Messages have been transferred or the
2871 GSME decides to stop requesting Messages.
2872 When the GSME wishes to send a Message, the GSME sends a TransferData command to
2873 the CHF with the PUT structure in the Tunnel Manager Header and the Message in the
2874 remainder of the Data field in the TransferData command.
2875 TransferData commands sent between GSME and CHF
2876 When it wishes to send a Message, so an Alert or Response or GBT Message, a GSME shall
2877 send a TransferData command to the CHF with the value in the Data parameter payload of
2878 the TransferData command set to the concatenation:
2879 0x03 || Message
2880 When it wishes to retrieve a Message stored for it on a CHF, a GSME shall send a
2881 TransferData command to the CHF with the value in the Data field set to 0x01. When the
2882 CHF receives such a TransferData command from a GSME, the CHF shall send a TransferData
2883 command to the GSME with the value in the Data parameter payload set to:
2884 the concatenation
2885 0x02 || (Number of Messages remaining for retrieval after this Message) || (Message
2886 addressed to the GSME)
2887
2888 where it has Messages for the GSME not yet downloaded by the GSME; or
Page 149

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
2889 the concatenation 0x02 || 0x00, where it has no Messages for the GSME to retrieve, the
2890 0x00 representing the number of Messages available to retrieve.
2891 GSME and GPF interactions
2892 Introduction – informative
2893 The GSME is informed that Remote Party or SME.C.PPMID-GSME Commands are available
2894 for it to retrieve via Tunnel Message Pending flag on the GPF.
2895 The GSME should, under normal operating circumstances, retrieve all Commands buffered
2896 for it when it turns its HAN Interface on. For example, if two Commands are buffered for it,
2897 the GSME should retrieve both Commands before turning its HAN Interface off.
2898 However, in some circumstances, a GSME may choose not to retrieve all buffered
2899 Commands in a single session. In such cases, the GSME should retrieve each Command as
2900 soon as possible after that Command is received by the CHF.
2901 Potential reasons for a GSME failing to retrieve all buffered Commands include:
2902 the GSME battery requires time to recover;
2903 the GSME is entering a ‘low battery’ mode and limiting the use of its radio; or
2904 a radio communications error.
2905 Section 10.3 details actions the CHF may take where Commands, or GBT Messages
2906 containing parts of Commands, for a GSME are not retrieved by the GSME.
2907 Commands addressed to a GSME must be processed by the GSME and, when successfully
2908 processed, any changed operational or configuration data must be made available to the GPF.
2909 The GPF then has updated information to provide to other Devices on the same SMHAN.
2910 In ZSE terms, the GPF incorporates two distinct logical Devices, which are discoverable and
2911 addressed on different endpoints. Section 7 describes which clusters reside on which
2912 endpoint.
2913 GSME data residing on the ZigBee Gas Mirror Endpoint – informative
2914 The ZigBee Gas Mirror Endpoint provides a ‘reflection’ of the data held by the GSME. A
2915 GSME is typically a battery-powered Device and its HAN Interface is mostly not turned on,
2916 making it unable to respond to other Devices. The GSME turns its HAN Interface on at
2917 regular intervals (e.g. 30 minutes) and pushes consumption data to the ZigBee Gas Mirror
2918 Endpoint. This provides other Devices on the same SMHAN with access to GSME
2919 consumption data at any time.
2920 GSME data residing on the ZigBee Gas ESI Endpoint – informative
Page 150

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
2921 The ZigBee Gas ESI Endpoint holds GSME data which is provided by a Remote Party, for
2922 example pricing. The ZigBee Gas ESI Endpoint makes this type of data available to Devices
2923 on the same SMHAN.
2924 GSME data from a Remote Party is sent to the GSME in a Remote Party Command. Such a
2925 Command has to be validated by the GSME before any data in it is applied by the GSME. For
2926 example, a Command to change tariff must be rejected by the GSME if it fails authentication,
2927 and the data in the Command must not be applied in such circumstances.
2928 If data in a Remote Party Command is accepted by the GSME, a mechanism is needed to
2929 provide the changed data to the ZigBee Gas ESI Endpoint. This is so that the ZigBee Gas ESI
2930 Endpoint can then provide that data to other Devices on the same SMHAN.
2931 A mechanism is also needed to deal with a Response not being received from the GSME.
2932 The lack of a Response may indicate that the GSME and the ZigBee Gas ESI Endpoint do not
2933 contain the same value in one or more data items. If data items on the two are not
2934 synchronised, Devices on the SMHAN will display incorrect information.
2935 There are several possible reasons why this lack of a Response may arise, not all of which
2936 mean that data is out of synchronisation:
2937 the Command has failed validation by the GSME and has been discarded;
2938 the Response has been lost due to a communications error; or
2939 a software error.
2940 GSME Command retrieval and TOM Requirements
2941 TOM Commands and Responses
2942 A Command shall be a TOM Command if it is a Remote Party Command with one of the
2943 following Message Codes:
2944 0x006B (GCS01a Set Tariff and Price on GSME);
2945 0x006F (GCS05 Update Prepayment Configurations on GSME) – the GPF shall only process
2946 the Calendar cluster ZSE commands within the Command;
2947 0x0071 (GCS07 Send Message to GSME);
2948 0x0015 (CS11 Clear ZigBee Device Event Log) where the Command is addressed to the
2949 GSME;
2950 0x007C (GCS23 Set CV and Conversion Factor Value(s) on the GSME);
2951 0x007E (GCS25 Set Billing Calendar on the GSME);
2952 0x00D8 (GCS25a Set Billing Calendar on the GSME – all periodicities);
Page 151

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
2953 0x0088 (GCS44 Write Contact Details on GSME); or
2954 0x00A3 (GCS01b Set Price on GSME).
2955 A TOM Response shall be a Response to a TOM Command.
2956 For clarity, neither a TOM Response nor a TOM Command may contain Encrypted data.
2957 Processing of Commands addressed to a GSME
2958 The CHF, GPF and GSME shall undertake the processing steps below following receipt of a
2959 Remote Party or SME.C.PPMID-GSME Command by the Communications Hub, where that
2960 Command is addressed to a GSME on the same SMHAN:
2961 1. the CHF shall buffer the Command and instruct the GPF to set the Tunnel Message
2962 Pending flag to inform the GSME that the Command is awaiting retrieval. If the
2963 Command has been sent as multiple GBT Messages, the GPF Tunnel Message Pending
2964 flag shall only be set once all GBT Messages making up the Command have been
2965 received by the Communications Hub. If not all GBT Messages making up a Command
2966 have been received by a Communications Hub within 24 hours of the first GBT Message
2967 in that Command being received, then the CHF may discard the GBT Messages that have
2968 been received for that command;
2969 2. if 24 hours elapse after setting the GPF Tunnel Message Pending flag without the
2970 Command being retrieved by the GSME, the CHF may discard the Command. If the CHF
2971 discards a Command in this way, it shall notify the GPF and the GPF shall log the event in
2972 its Event Log and send an Alert with a GBZ Payload containing an Alert Code 0x819D;
2973 1. when the GSME turns its HAN Interface on, it shall read the Tunnel Message Pending
2974 flag and retrieve the Command using the TransferData command as defined in
2975 Section 10.2.3. Each TransferData command received by the GSME shall result in the
2976 GSME sending a DefaultResponse command;
2977 2. the CHF shall process the DefaultResponse commands it receives to establish when
2978 the Command has successfully been retrieved by the GSME, and shall provide an
2979 indication to the GPF accordingly. The GPF shall, when there are no further
2980 Commands or GBT Messages pending retrieval by the GSME, clear the Tunnel
2981 Message Pending flag;
2982 3. if a Command is a TOM Command, the CHF shall retain a copy of the Command
2983 contents. For each such Command, the CHF shall start a response timer at the point
2984 where it has received DefaultResponse command(s) confirming the GSME has
2985 successfully retrieved the Command;
2986 4. once a Command is successfully retrieved by the GSME, the GSME shall process the
2987 Command in line with the requirements of the GBCS. Note that (1) this processing
Page 152

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
2988 shall result in the GSME attempting to send a Response to the Command or an Alert
2989 that it has received an invalid Command and (2) if sending a Response, the Response
2990 shall, as per the GBCS requirements, detail the success or failure of GSME processing
2991 for each instruction within the corresponding Command;
2992 5. the GSME shall not, under normal operating conditions, delay sending the Response
2993 and shall, where possible, send it before turning its HAN Interface off;
2994 6. on receipt of a Response that is a TOM Response, the CH shall inspect the Response
2995 from the GSME. If the Response indicates successful execution of at least one
2996 elemental ZCL / ZSE command in the corresponding TOM Command, the CHF shall
2997 transfer a copy of the corresponding TOM Command contents and the TOM
2998 Response to the GPF, and shall clear the response timer for the Command;
2999 7. on receipt of a TOM Response and the corresponding TOM Command contents, the
3000 GPF shall clear any stored copy it has of a TOM Command and then:
3001 if the TOM Command is not future dated, process the elemental ZCL / ZSE commands
3002 contained within the Command according to the status within the Response, updating data
3003 it holds accordingly. Once processed by the GPF, the GPF shall make any updated data
3004 available over the WAN and over the HAN to the Devices in the GPF’s Device Log;
3005 if the TOM Command is future dated, store a copy of the TOM Command without updating
3006 any data it makes available over the WAN or HAN;
3007 8. if a Response to a TOM Command has not been received by the Communications
3008 Hub when the corresponding response timer reaches 6 hours:
3009 the CHF may discard its copy of the TOM Command contents, clear the response timer and
3010 notify the GPF accordingly; and
3011 on receipt of such a notification, the GPF shall log the event in its Event Log and send an
3012 Alert with a GBZ Payload containing an Alert Code 0x819E;
3013 9. for clarity, the CHF shall relay all Remote Party Responses received on its HAN
3014 Interface through the WAN Interface;
3015 10. whenever the CHF receives an Alert detailing activation of a future dated ZCL / ZSE
3016 command from within a TOM Command (so an Alert with Alert Code 0x8F66 where
3017 the Message Code in the Alert Payload is 0x006B or 0x00A3), the CHF shall pass a
3018 copy of that Alert to the GPF;
3019 11. on receipt of such an Alert the GPF shall compare the Originator Counter in the Alert
3020 Payload with the Originator Counter of any copy of a TOM Command it holds with
3021 the same Message Code as in the Alert Payload, and:
Page 153

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3022 if the Originator Counters match, the GPF shall update the data it shares over the HAN and
3023 WAN with the elemental ZCL / ZSE command contained within the TOM Command; or
3024 if the Originator Counters do not match or the GPF does not hold a TOM Command with this
3025 Message Code, the GPF shall send an Alert with Alert Code 0x819E, as specified by Section
3026 16.
3027 GPF Structured Data Items
3028 Underlined terms in this Section 10.4 shall have their meaning in the SMETS and / or CHTS.
3029 Introduction – informative
3030 There are GPF requirements to store structured data items which do not have a direct one to
3031 one mapping in ZSE, or the interpretation may be uncertain. These structured data items
3032 have to be constructed by the GPF.
3033 Structured Data Items
3034 This Section 10.4.2 details how each structured data item shall be constructed by the GPF.
3035 Daily Read Log
3036 The GSME shall record the Daily Read Log data items at midnight UTC as defined in SMETS.
3037 The GSME shall use the snapshot cause ‘General’ (0x00000001) for the snapshot taken.
3038 The GSME shall push the snapshot to the GPF using the PublishSnapshot command with a
3039 SnapshotPayloadType and a SnapshotSub-Payload populated in line with the requirements
3040 of Use Case ‘GCS16a Read GSME Daily Read log(s)’. It is not necessary for the GSME to
3041 report any attributes which duplicate those contained in the snapshot.
3042 The GPF shall populate the relevant attributes upon receipt of the PublishSnapshot
3043 command, providing the command is received between midnight (UTC) and the next
3044 scheduled wake of the GSME.
3045 The GPF shall store the data contained in the PublishSnapshot command in the GPF copy of
3046 the GSME Daily Read Log.
3047 In the event of a communications outage, the GPF shall retrieve missing snapshots using the
3048 GetSnapshot command, with the UTC start time field populated based on the last received
3049 snapshot timestamp, if one has been received.
3050 Prepayment Daily Read Log
3051 If the GSME is operating in prepayment mode it shall record the Prepayment Daily Read Log
3052 data items at midnight UTC. In ZSE terms, the GSME shall take a prepayment snapshot of
3053 the relevant items. The format and data of the prepayment snapshot taken is defined in ZSE.
Page 154

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3054 The GSME shall use the snapshot cause ‘General’ (0x00000001) for the prepayment
3055 snapshot taken.
3056 The GSME shall push the prepayment snapshot to the GPF using the Publish Prepay
3057 Snapshot command.
3058 The GPF shall populate the relevant attributes upon receipt of the Publish Prepay Snapshot
3059 command, providing the command is received between midnight (UTC) and the next
3060 scheduled wake of the GSME.
3061 The GPF shall store the data contained in the Publish Prepay Snapshot command in the GPF
3062 copy of the GSME Prepayment Daily Read Log.
3063 In the event of a communications outage, the GPF shall retrieve missing prepayment
3064 snapshots using the GetPrepaySnapshot command (and GetPrepaySnapshot notification
3065 flag) with the UTC start time field populated based on the last received prepayment
3066 snapshot timestamp, if one has been received.
3067 Billing Data Log – informative
3068 SMETS defines Billing Data Log as a log capable of storing the following UTC date and time
3069 stamped entries:
3070 twelve entries comprising Tariff TOU Register Matrix, the Consumption Register and Tariff
3071 Block Counter Matrix;
3072 five entries comprising the value of prepayment credits;
3073 ten entries comprising the value of payment-based debt payments; and
3074 twelve entries comprising Meter Balance, Emergency Credit Balance, Accumulated Debt
3075 Register, Payment Debt Register and Time Debt Registers [1 … 2].
3076 Requirements for each part are detailed separately in the following Sections.
3077 Billing Data Log – Tariff TOU Register Matrix, the Consumption Register and Tariff Block
3078 Counter Matrix
3079 The GSME shall capture this snapshot at the following trigger points:
3080 End of Billing Cycle (snapshot cause ‘End of Billing Period’ );
3081 Change of Payment Mode (snapshot cause ‘Change of Meter Mode’);
3082 Change of Tariff (snapshot cause ‘Change of Tariff Information’); and
3083 as specified in Section 13.3.5.10 (snapshot cause ‘Change of Supplier’).
Page 155

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3084 When it next turns on its HAN Interface, the GSME shall push this snapshot to the GPF using
3085 the PublishSnapshot Command with a SnapshotPayloadType and a SnapshotSub-Payload
3086 populated in line with the requirements of Use Case ‘GCS15b Read GSME Billing Data Log
3087 (change of mode / tariff triggered)’.
3088 The GPF shall store the data contained in the PublishSnapshot command in the GPF copy of
3089 the GSME Billing data Log.
3090 In the event of a communications outage, the GPF shall retrieve missing snapshots using the
3091 GetSnapshot command (and the relevant notification flag) with the UTC start time field
3092 populated based on the last received snapshot timestamp, if one has been received, or
3093 0x0000 otherwise.
3094 Billing Data Log – value of prepayment credits
3095 Upon completion of processing of a valid Prepayment Top Up, the GSME shall push the
3096 Prepayment Top Up’s details to the GPF using the PublishTop Up Log command.
3097 The GPF shall store the data contained in the Publish Top Up Log command in the GPF copy
3098 of the GSME Billing data Log.
3099 If there has been a communications outage, the GPF shall use the Get Top Up Log command
3100 to retrieve all Prepayment Top Ups that may have been processed during the
3101 communications outage. The GSME shall set the Date / Time field of the Get Top Up Log
3102 command to the current UTC time.
3103 Billing Data Log – payment-based debt payments
3104 Upon completion of processing of a valid Prepayment Top Up where the GSME has made a
3105 debt payment using part of that Prepayment Top Up, the GSME shall push details of that
3106 debt payment only to the GPF using the Publish Debt Log command.
3107 The GPF shall record the details provided in the GPF copy of the GSME Billing Data Log.
3108 In cases of communications outages, the GPF shall request any outstanding payment-based
3109 debt payments by use of the GetDebtRepaymentLog command (and GetDebtRepaymentLog
3110 notification flag) with the Debt Type field set to 0x02 (Debt 3).
3111 Billing Data Log – Meter Balance, Emergency Credit Balance, Accumulated Debt Register,
3112 Payment Debt Register and Time Debt Registers [1 … 2]
3113 The GSME shall capture this snapshot at the following trigger points:
3114 End of Billing Cycle (snapshot cause bit 1 set: ‘End of Billing Period’ , as per PublishSnapshot
3115 command);
3116 Change of Payment Mode (snapshot cause bit 14 set: ‘Change of Meter Mode’);

3117 Change of Tariff (snapshot cause including set: bit 3 ‘Change of Tariff Information’); and
3118 as specified in Section 13.3.5.10 (snapshot cause ‘Change of Supplier’).
3119 When it next turns on its HAN Interface, the GSME shall push this snapshot to the GPF using
3120 the Publish Prepay Snapshot command.
3121 The GPF shall store the data contained in the Publish Prepay Snapshot command in the GPF
3122 copy of the GSME Billing Data Log.
3123 In the event of a communications outage, the GPF shall retrieve missing snapshots using the
3124 GetPrepaySnapshot command (and GetPrepaySnapshot notification flag) with the UTC start
3125 time field populated based on the last received snapshot timestamp, if one has been
3126 received.
3127 GPF Profile Data Log
3128 The GPF shall create the GPF Profile Data Log from the consumption information pushed by
3129 the GSME each half hour.
3130 The GSME shall, on each half hour, record the following information and push to the GPF:
3131 the CurrentSummationDelivered attribute containing total consumption value (with units of
3132 m3);
3133 the CurrentDayAlternativeConsumptionDelivered attribute containing total consumption
3134 today (with units of kWh); and
3135 the CurrentDayCostConsumptionDelivered attribute containing total cost of consumption
3136 today (with units of Currency Unit);
3137 Upon receipt of the pushed data, the GPF shall calculate the consumption with units of m3
3138 over the previous half hour by subtracting its previously recorded total consumption value
3139 from the total consumption value now sent.
3140 The resulting value shall be stored in the GPF Profile Data Log.
3141 In the event that there are missing values in the GPF Profile Data Log, the GPF shall
3142 interrogate the GSME Profile Data Log using the GetSampledData (SampleID 0x0000)
3143 command and the GetSampledData notification flag to retrieve missing values.
3144 GPF Daily Gas Consumption Log
3145 The GPF shall create the GPF Daily Gas Consumption Log based on the values pushed from
3146 the GSME. The difference between last total consumption value pushed from the GSME
3147 each UTC day and the last value pushed in the prior UTC day shall be time stamped and
3148 stored in the GPF Daily Gas Consumption Log, so that the values in the log represent
3149 consumption in that UTC day.

3150 In the event of communications outages resulting in the final daily value being missed, the
3151 GPF shall retrieve the values from the GSME Profile Data Log using the GetSampledData
3152 (SampleID 0x0000) command and GetSampledData notification flag.
3153 Historical Attributes
3154 A GSME shall support:
3155 the Historical Cost Consumption Information attribute set, measured in Currency Units; and
3156 the Alternative Historical Consumption attribute set, measured in kWh.
3157 A GPF shall mirror the attribute sets listed above.
3158 As per Section 10.4.2.8, the GSME shall, on each half hour, record the following information
3159 and push to the GPF:
3160 total consumption value (with units of m3);
3161 total consumption today (with units of kWh); and
3162 total cost of consumption today (with units of Currency Unit);
3163 Using the ‘total consumption today’ value, the GPF shall update the attributes of the
3164 mirrored Alternative Historical Consumption attribute set.
3165 Using the ‘total cost of consumption today’ value, the GPF shall update the attributes of the
3166 mirrored Historical Cost Consumption Information attribute set.
3167 In exception circumstances, the GPF shall request the GSME to push the historical data sets
3168 using the ‘Push Historical Metering Data Attribute Set and ‘Push Historical Prepayment Data
3169 Attribute Set’ notification flags. The GSME shall interpret the ‘Push Historical Metering Data
3170 Attribute Set’ notification flag as requiring it to push the Alternative Historical Consumption
3171 attribute set.

3309 GCS16b and the ZSE requirement that the ‘Latest End Time’ is the ‘latest time of a snapshot
3310 to be returned by a corresponding Publish Snapshot command’, when processing a Get
3311 Snapshot or Get Prepay Snapshot command, either from another GPF or as part of a Remote
3312 Party Command, a GPF shall return all snapshots with a timestamp up to and including the
3313 date-time in the Latest End Time parameter.

3314 For clarity and in line with the requirements of Use Cases CS10a and CS10b, when

3322 Hand Held Terminal (HHT) interactions
3323 Introduction – informative
3324 An HHT allows for delivery of Remote Party Messages to and from the SMHAN. This is as an
3325 alternative delivery route to the Communications Hub’s WAN connection. It is intended for
3326 one-off configuration of Devices, for example at installation. Hence, there are time outs to
3327 ensure usage is limited in this way.
3328 This Section 10.5 specifies requirements related to:
3329 how a connection is made between an HHT and a Communications Hub; and
3330 how Remote Party Messages are then to be transferred to and from the HHT.
3331 Establishing a connection between an HHT and a Communications Hub – informative
3332 ZigBee supports an Inter-PAN mechanism which can be used for communication links
3333 between Devices. This mechanism is used to establish a link key between the HHT and the
3334 Communications Hub (referred to as the Inter-PAN Link Key (IPLK)), by using ZSE’s CBKE (for
3335 clarity, this IPLK is not used to encrypt any Inter-PAN communication). The Inter-PAN link is
3336 then used for HHT to Communications Hub communication:
3337 the HHT uses the link to send its Entity Identifier and Install Code to the Communications
3338 Hub as part of a ‘CCS01 Add Device to CHF device log’ Command;
3339 the Communications Hub adds these details to the CHF’s Device Log (so allowing the HHT to
3340 join the SMHAN) and confirms this to the HHT using a ‘CCS01 Add Device to CHF device log’
3341 Response; and
3342 the HHT then joins the SMHAN and so can exchange Remote Party Messages within the
3343 Communications Hub, and the Communications Hub can relay them to / from the specified
3344 Device(s) on the HAN. The IPLK is used as the pre-configured link key in this joining process.
3345 Both the Inter-PAN communications and joining to the SMHAN use the CBKE mechanism that
3346 is defined in ZSE.
Page 163

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3347 Inter-PAN is only to be available for 60 minutes from power on of the Communications Hub.
3348 So, if needed, Inter-PAN can be enabled by power cycling the Communications Hub.
3349 The Inter-PAN mechanism defined by ZSE requires the HHT to specify the Communications
3350 Hub that it wishes to link to. There may be multiple Communications Hubs available to the
3351 HHT to connect to via Inter-PAN.
3352 There are a number of options to provide the HHT with information sufficient to identify
3353 uniquely the Communications Hub it is to link to, including:
3354 the installer manually reading the GPF’s Entity Identifier (which is the IEEE address of the
3355 Communications Hub’s SMHAN radio) printed on the Hub, and confirming / selecting this on
3356 the HHT; or
3357 the installer using a scanner on the HHT to read the GPF’s Entity Identifier.
3358 Two illustrative connection scenarios are provided in the following two Sections
3359 Illustration 1: Installer manually chooses network – informative
3360 1. the Communications Hub opens Inter-PAN communication for 60 minutes after
3361 power on;
3362 2. the HHT is powered on;
3363 3. the HHT performs an active scan using the Beacon Request mechanism;
3364 4. the HHT displays the IEEE addresses returned in the Beacons from all neighbouring
3365 PAN Coordinators. Note that the GBCS requires the Extended PAN ID initially to be
3366 set to the Communications Hub’s HAN Interface’s IEEE address. This is the same as
3367 the GPF Entity Identifier, which is printed on the Communications Hub in line with
3368 CHTS. Note that, if the Communications Hub is a replacement for one previously
3369 installed, the Extended PAN ID will not be its GPF Entity Identifier, and the installer
3370 will need a different way to establish the correct Extended PAN ID to use;
3371 5. the installer (who knows the Consumer’s Communications Hub’s ZigBee IEEE address
3372 as the GPF Entity Identifier is printed on the Communications Hub) picks the desired
3373 IEEE address;
3374 6. the HHT initiates Inter-PAN CBKE with the Communications Hub;
3375 7. the Communications Hub responds to the Inter-PAN CBKE;
3376 8. if Inter-PAN CBKE completes successfully, the HHT sends its Install Code and Entity
3377 Identifier to the Communications Hub in a CCS01 Command, then
3378 9. the Communications Hub adds the HHT to the CHF Device Log and sends a CCS01
3379 Response to the HHT accordingly, and then
Page 164

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3380 10. the HHT joins to the SMHAN;
3381 11. otherwise, no link is established.
3382 Illustration 2: HHT uses barcode scan – informative
3383 1. the Communications Hub opens Inter-PAN communication for 60 minutes after
3384 power on;
3385 2. the HHT is powered on;
3386 3. the HHT optically scans the GPF Entity Identifier printed on the target
3387 Communications Hub;
3388 4. the HHT performs an active scan using the Beacon Request mechanism;
3389 5. when a Beacon returns an IEEE address equal to the scanned GPF Entity Identifier,
3390 the HHT initiates Inter-PAN communication with the Communications Hub so
3391 identified;
3392 6. the Communications Hub responds to the Inter-PAN CBKE;
3393 7. if Inter-PAN CBKE completes successfully:
3394 8. the HHT sends its Install Code and Entity Identifier to the Communications Hub in a
3395 CCS01 Command, then
3396 9. the Communications Hub adds the HHT to the CHF Device Log and sends a CCS01
3397 Response to the HHT accordingly, and then
3398 10. the HHT joins to the SMHAN;
3399 11. otherwise, no link is established.
3400 WAN proxy operation
3401 Introduction – informative
3402 The HHT has to be capable of holding Remote Party Messages, to which the appropriate
3403 Remote Party Message protection has already been applied, and has to be capable of
3404 exchanging such Messages.
3405 The Communications Hub must therefore be able to maintain two interfaces to the WAN;
3406 the real one via the WAN Interface and a ‘logical WAN’ via the connection to the HHT.
3407 WAN Responses
3408 The Communications Hub shall send any Responses and Alerts through both its WAN
3409 Interface and the link to the HHT, if present. Whilst this may result in apparent unsolicited
Page 165

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3410 Responses at the Remote Party which have to be dealt with, it ensures the earliest possible
3411 reconciliation of Commands destined for Smart Metering Equipment.
3412 HHT and CHF – Device Requirements
3413 Any Device which provided its Entity Identifier and Install Code in a CCS01 Command to the
3414 Communications Hub via Inter-PAN shall be treated by the CHF as being of type HHT. For
3415 clarity, the Device Type specified in any such CCS01 Command shall be disregarded by the
3416 CHF.
3417 As per Section 10.2.2, in interactions between an HHT and a Communications Hub over the
3418 SMHAN:
3419 the HHT shall support the Tunneling Cluster as a Client; and
3420 the Communications Hub shall support the Tunneling Cluster as a Server.
3421 The Communications Hub shall only allow Inter-PAN communications for 60 minutes from
3422 any power on of the Communications Hub. For clarity, this is the period during which an
3423 HHT can establish a connection, not the period of use of any connection.
3424 At power on, a Communications Hub shall remove any Devices of type HHT from the CHF
3425 Device Log.
3426 The Communications Hub shall prior to installation, set nwkExtendedPANId to be the Entity
3427 Identifier of the GPF, which is always the Communications Hub’s IEEE address for its HAN
3428 Interface.
3429 HHT and CHF – establishing communications
3430 Prior to being able to exchange Messages, the HHT and Communications Hub shall
3431 undertake the following steps:
3432 1. the HHT shall identify the Communications Hub and initiate the CBKE process using
3433 Inter-PAN communications, as specified in this Section 10.5.3.4;
3434 the Communications Hub shall not respond to any such communications if more than 60
3435 minutes has elapsed since the Communications Hub’s most recent power on, or if there is a
3436 Device of type HHT already in the CHF’s Device Log. Otherwise, the Communications Hub
3437 shall respond to the CBKE request;
3438 if CBKE does not succeed, processing shall cease. Otherwise, the Communications Hub and
3439 HHT shall each store the link key established through CBKE (referred to as the Inter-PAN Link
3440 Key (IPLK)) along with a record of the other Device’s Entity Identifier, which is its IEEE
3441 address. Then processing shall continue from step 4;
Page 166

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3442 the HHT shall send a ‘CCS01 Add Device to CHF device log’ Command, populated with the
3443 HHT’s Entity Identifier and Install Code, to the CHF using the mechanism defined in Section
3444 10.5.3.5;
3445 where all parts of the Command are successfully received, the CHF shall first validate that
3446 the Entity Identifier in the CCS01 Command matches the Entity Identifier it stored against
3447 the IPLK at step 3. If it does not match, processing shall cease. Otherwise the CHF shall
3448 process the Command according to the requirements of the ‘CCS01 Add Device to CHF
3449 device log’ Use Case, and shall send any resulting ‘CCS01 Add Device to CHF device log’
3450 Response to the HHT, via Inter-PAN using the mechanism defined in Section 10.5.3.5. For
3451 clarity the Install Code in the CCS01 Command shall not be used in the subsequent ZigBee
3452 joining. Where the CHF sends such a Response, it shall start a timer. When that timer
3453 reaches 0xFFFF seconds, the CHF shall remove the HHT from its Device Log, remove the HHT
3454 from the SMHAN and close any open tunnels to the HHT;
3455 if the ‘CCS01 Add Device to CHF device log’ Response from the CHF to the HHT states that
3456 the HHT has been added to the CHF’s Device Log, the HHT may attempt to join the SMHAN.
3457 The Devices shall use the IPLK stored at step 3 as the pre-configured link key to secure the
3458 joining process. If the joining is successful:
3459 1. the HHT shall send a RequestTunnel command to the CHF, with contents as per
3460 Section 10.2.2;
3461 the CHF shall process the RequestTunnel command and send a RequestTunnelResponse
3462 command in response; and
3463 if TunnelStatus in the RequestTunnelResponse command is not 0x00 (‘success’),
3464 processing by the HHT shall cease. Otherwise the HHT and CHF may now exchange
3465 Messages using the TransferData command with the TunnelID associated with
3466 ProtocolID 6.
3467 Note that steps 1 to 5 above use Inter-PAN communications; the remaining step 6 uses the
3468 standard ZigBee SMHAN communications.
3469 Once the HHT has joined the SMHAN, any Messages received by the CHF from the HHT in
3470 the Data parameter payload of a TransferData command with the TunnelID associated with
3471 ProtocolID 6, shall be forwarded to the relevant Device on the SMHAN as if they were
3472 received via the Communications Hub’s WAN Interface. If any such Message contains a
3473 Business Target ID which is not in the CHF Device Log and is not the CHF ID or the GPF ID, the
3474 Communications Hub may silently discard the Message.
3475 Whilst the HHT is in the CHF’s Device Log and joined to the SMHAN, any Responses received
3476 by the CHF from any SMHAN Device shall be provided to the HHT using the TransferData
Page 167

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3477 command with the TunnelID associated with ProtocolID 6. Such Responses shall also be sent
3478 over the Communications Hub’s WAN Interface, if available.
3479 Note that the requirements of Section 7.2.11(Transfer of Large Remote Party Messages)
3480 apply to Messages exchanged once the HHT has joined the SMHAN. Section 7.2.11
3481 requirements do not apply to the CCS01 Command and Response exchanged using the Inter-
3482 PAN mechanism.
3483 Once the HHT usage on the SMHAN is complete, the HHT should send a CloseTunnel
3484 command to the Communications Hub. On receipt of such a CloseTunnel command from an
3485 HHT, the Communications Hub shall process that command as per the ZSE specification and
3486 shall:
3487 remove the HHT from its Device Log; and
3488 remove the HHT from the SMHAN.
3489 Population of the Inter-PAN ZigBee Frame
3490 A Device may send a Remote Party Message to another Device on the same SM HAN using
3491 the ZSE Inter-PAN Frame. In doing so, the sending Device shall:
3492 Take the ‘n’ most significant octets of the Remote Party Message to create an ‘Inter-PAN
3493 Message Fragment (IPMF)’, where ‘n’ is the maximum number such that the
3494 aMaxPHYPacketSize (with its IEEE 802.15.4 2003 specification meaning) would not be
3495 exceeded in the resulting message over the SM HAN. This IPMF shall have an index of 0x00;
3496 If there are remaining octets in the Remote Party Message, take the next ‘n’ most significant
3497 octets to create IPMF with an index of one greater than the previous IPMF;
3498 Repeat step 2 until there are no remaining octets in the Remote Party Message; and
3499 Set the ‘Total Number of IPMF’ to be the number of IPMF so created.
3500 A Device receiving a Remote Party Message by this mechanism shall respond to each IPMF
3501 received with an ‘IPMF Response’ constructed according to this Section10.5.3.5. The
3502 receiving Device shall re-construct the Remote Party Message in a way that is aligned with
3503 the splitting mechanism defined in this Section10.5.3.5.
3504 If a response to an Inter-PAN ZigBee Frame is required by this Section 10.5.3.5 but the
3505 receiving Device has not received such a Response after 60 seconds, the receiving Device
3506 may treat the transmission of the underlying CCS01 Message as having failed.
3507 When a sending Device is populating the Inter-PAN ZigBee Frame to communicate with a
3508 receiving Device using Inter-PAN, the sending Device shall:

3661 CHF functional requirements – Sub GHz Channel Scan actions
3662 The CH shall complete a Sub GHz Channel Scan.
3663 The CHF shall then set ‘Alternative Sub GHz Channel’ to:
3664 The channel which, of the Sub GHz Channels scanned, has the lowest noise, if this lowest
3665 noise channel is different than the CH Operating Sub GHz Channel or if there is no existing
3666 channel recorded in the CH Operating Sub GHz Channel; or
3667 The channel which, of the Sub GHz Channels scanned, has the second lowest noise, if the
3668 lowest noise channel is the CH Operating Sub GHz Channel.
3669 The CHF shall then set ‘Relative Noise’ to be the SMHAN radio noise difference in decibels
3670 between the CH Operating Sub GHz Channel and the ‘Alternative Sub GHz Channel’, or to be
3671 zero if there is no existing channel recorded in the CH Operating Sub GHz Channel.
3672 The CHF shall then determine whether to change Sub GHz Channel according to Table
3673 10.6.2.8, the value of scanTrigger and the ‘Relative Noise’.
3674 The CHF shall comply with the ZSE requirements whenever undertaking a channel change.
3675 Additionally, having set the Channel Change Pending Functional Notification flag, the CH
3676 shall wait until the soonest of either:
3677 The GSME has read the Channel Change attribute; or
3678 60 minutes have elapsed
3679 before changing its Operating Sub GHz Channel.
3680 Where the CHF has changed the Operating Sub GHz Channel, the CHF shall:
3681 1. create an entry in the Sub GHz Channel Log with Event Code set to 0x8F26 and
3682 otherInfo set to the concatenation (value of Operating Sub GHz Channel) || 0x0901
3683 || scanTrigger; and

3691 Sub GHz End Devices - functional requirements
3692 A Sub GHz End Device shall:
Page 192

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3693 not act as a ZigBee router when operating on a Sub GHz Channel;
3694 where the Device can also support 2.4 GHz operation:
3695 on first connecting to a ZigBee network, attempt to establish network communication in the
3696 2.4GHz band. Only where communications are not of sufficient quality, shall the Device
3697 attempt to establish network communications in the Sub GHz band; and
3698 having connected to a ZigBee network at either 2.4 GHz or at Sub GHz, not attempt to
3699 change to the other of 2.4 GHz or Sub GHz; and
3700 not use the Mgmt_NWK_Unsolicited_Enhanced_Update_notify command to notify the CH
3701 of problems with its communications link more frequently than once in any 30-minute
3702 period.
3703 Sub GHz GSME - functional requirements
3704 Sub GHz GSME shall wait at least 2 hours from detecting SMHAN interference before
3705 indicating that the interference is continuing by way of sending a
3706 Mgmt_NWK_Unsolicited_Enhanced_Update_notify command to the CH.
3707 When operating on Sub GHz, GSME shall, on each wake up, check the Functional Notification
3708 Flags for bits 25 (Energy Scan Pending) and 26 (Channel Change Pending).
3709 If either bit is set (so has a value 0b1) then the GSME shall attempt to retrieve any
3710 Commands buffered for it on the CH before turning off its SMHAN radio. For clarity and in
3711 line with Section 10.6.2.8, the GSME should attempt such retrieval before reading the CHF
3712 Channel Change attribute, if it is to maximise the likelihood of Command retrieval before it
3713 turns off its SMHAN radio.
3714 If bit 25 is set, the GSME shall disable the SMETS User Interface Commands ‘4.5.2.4 Check
3715 for HAN Interface Commands’ and ‘4.5.2.8 Find Smart Metering Home Area Network and Re-
3716 establish Communications Links’ and shall not receive and execute ‘4.5.3.3 Add Credit’ and
3717 ‘4.5.3.1 Activate Emergency Credit’ Commands from a PPMID and a Gas Proxy Function
3718 (where those terms have their SMETS meanings), as required by SMETS 4.4.7.2, until it next
3719 turns on its SMHAN radio.
3720 Note that CH may change Sub GHz Channel once every 24 hours to attempt to communicate
3721 with a lost GSME. On each such change, the CH will undertake a Sub GHz Channel Scan,
3722 meaning that it cannot communicate with a GSME for a period of time. GSME should factor
3723 both the 24 hour period and the associated Sub GHz Channel Scan in to their attempts to re-

3728 SMHAN management
3729 Requests to leave the SMHAN
3730 Where a Device is not a ZigBee end device or a Communications Hub, the
3731 nwkLeaveRequestAllowed attribute of the NIB (Network layer information base) shall be set
3732 to FALSE. This means that, in line with the ZigBee specification, Leave commands received
3733 by such Devices shall be immediately and silently discarded and such Devices shall not leave
3734 the SMHAN on receipt of such Leave commands.
3735 When a Device, which is a ZigBee end device, has received and executed a ZigBee Leave
3736 command with a value in the Rejoin Sub-Field of 0, the Device shall attempt to re-establish
3737 SMHAN communications using the ZSE 5.4.2 mechanisms.
3738 Network Key Change
3739 In line with the ‘ZigBee PRO/2007 Layer PICS and Stack Profiles’ requirement, Devices shall
3740 be capable of maintaining a minimum of two Network Keys.
3741 Whenever a CHF adds an Entity Identifier to, or removes an Entity Identifier from, its CHF
3742 Device Log, where the type of the Device to which that Entity Identifier relates is other than
3743 HHT or GPF, the CHF shall set a ‘CHF Device Log Changed Today’ flag.
3744 For clarity and in accordance with Section 10.5.3.3, any Device which provided its Entity
3745 Identifier and Install Code in a CCS01 Command to the Communications Hub via Inter-PAN
3746 shall be treated by the CHF as being of type HHT.
3747 Once each day, at a time between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC, the CHF shall check whether the
3748 ‘CHF Device Log Changed Today’ flag is set and, if it is set, the CHF shall take the following
3749 steps:
3750 1. generate a new Network Key;
3751 2. set, via the GPF, the Network Key Active flag in the FunctionalNotificationFlags and
3752 then wait for the soonest of (1) 60 minutes or (2) the GSME requesting the new
3753 Network Key;
3754 3. for each Device in the CHF Device Log which has an associated TC Link Key, unicast
3755 the new Network Key to the Device by issuing the APSME-TRANSPORT-KEY.request
3756 primitive with the DestAddress parameter set to the address of the Device and the
3757 communication to the Device being protected by the associated TC Link Key. The
3758 TransportKeyData sub-parameters shall be set as follows:
Page 194

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3759 1. the KeySeqNumber sub-parameter shall be set to the sequence count value for the
3760 new Network Key;
3761 2. The NetworkKey sub-parameter shall be set to the new Network Key; and
3762 3. The UseParent sub-parameter shall be set to FALSE;
3763 4. Send to all Devices in the CHF Device Log the APSMESWITCH-KEY.request primitive
3764 with the KeySeqNumber parameter set to the sequence count value for the new
3765 Network Key; and
3766 5. unset the ‘CHF Device Log Changed Today’ flag.
3767 Should any Device not receive the new Network Key and the instruction to switch to it, that
3768 Device will discover a communication failure. In such circumstances, the Device shall use
3769 the ZSE 5.4.2 (‘Re-joining a Secured Network’) mechanisms to re-establish communications.
3770 For clarity, the CHF shall not send the new Network Key to either:
3771 devices which have Entity Identifiers in the CHF Device Log but which do not have a TC Link
3772 Key established; or
3773 devices which do not have an Entity Identifier in the CHF Device Log.

3777 When a Device, which is not a CH, receives a new Network Key, the Device shall only store
3778 that Network Key where either:
3779 1. the Device does not currently hold any Network Key (so meaning it is being installed);
3780 or

3787 2. the Device’s nwkActiveKeySeqNumber is greater than 127 and the value of
3788 KeySeqNumber for the new Network Key is not greater than
3789 (nwkActiveKeySeqNumber + 128) modulo 256.

3888 VWD interactions
3889 VWD interactions shall only be allowed on a Virtual WAN CH.
3890 Introduction – informative
3891 A VWD allows for delivery of Messages to and from the SMHAN as an alternative delivery
3892 route to the Virtual WAN CH’s WAN connection. A VWD maintains a persistent connection
3893 with the Virtual WAN CH.
3894 This Section 10.9 specifies requirements related to:
3895 how a connection is made between a VWD and a Virtual WAN CH; and
3896 how Messages are then to be transferred to and from the VWD.
3897 Establishing a connection between a VWD and a Virtual WAN CH – informative
3898 A VWD may join the HAN in two ways:
Page 199

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3899 1. using the Inter-PAN mechanism in the same way as an HHT as per Section 10.5.3.4;
3900 or
3901 2. by a Remote Party adding the Entity Identifier of the VWD to the CHF Device Log
3902 using a CCS01 Command.
3903 If a VWD joins the HAN using the Inter-PAN mechanism, it initially behaves in exactly the
3904 same way as an HHT; in this case, the VWD is operating solely as an HHT. A VWD operates in
3905 ‘Virtual WAN mode’ after the CHF sends a RequestTunnel command to the VWD and the
3906 VWD sends a RequestTunnelResponse command in response with a TunnelStatus value of
3907 0x00 (‘Success’).
3908 If a VWD joins the HAN by a Remote Party using a CCS01 Command, the VWD behaves as the
3909 Device type it is added as, i.e. PPMID or Type 2.
3910 WAN proxy operation
3911 Introduction – informative
3912 The Virtual WAN CH maintains a WAN Interface via the WAN Communications Link and the
3913 Virtual WAN Communications Link. The WAN Communications Link is the link to the WAN
3914 Provider. The Virtual WAN Communications Link is a HAN connection to the VWD, ultimately
3915 connected to the Virtual WAN Provider.
3916 Active Communications Link
3917 The WAN Interface of a Virtual WAN CH shall only send and receive Messages on the active
3918 Communications Link, which is either the WAN Communications Link or the Virtual WAN
3919 Communications Link. The method used by the Virtual WAN CH to determine the active
3920 Communications Link is not prescribed in this document. For clarity, Messages that are used
3921 for link maintenance purposes maybe sent on either Communications Link at any time.
3922 VWD and CHF – Device Requirements
3923 A VWD that provides its Entity Identifier and Install Code in a CCS01 Command to the
3924 Communications Hub via Inter-PAN shall be treated by the CHF as being of type HHT as per
3925 Section 10.5.3.3.
3926 As per Section 10.2.2, in interactions between a VWD and a Virtual WAN CH over the
3927 SMHAN:
3928 the Virtual WAN CH shall support the Tunneling Cluster as a Client; and
3929 the VWD shall support the Tunneling Cluster as a Server.
3930 VWD and CHF – establishing communications via Inter-PAN
Page 200

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3931 The VWD and the Virtual WAN CH shall undertake Steps 1 to 6 as per Section 10.5.3.4. The
3932 VWD and CHF are now operating in ‘HHT mode’ and shall process any Message as described
3933 in Section 10.5.3.4.
3934 For the VWD and CHF to operate in ‘Virtual WAN mode’, the VWD forwards an ‘Enable
3935 Virtual WAN Device’ Command to the CHF using the TransferData command with the
3936 TunnelID associated with ProtocolID 6. The format of this Command and how it is processed
3937 is not described in this document.
3938 If the ‘Enable Virtual WAN Device’ Command is successfully processed:
3939 1. the CHF shall send a RequestTunnel command to the identified VWD using a
3940 ProtocolID of 0 (as per Section 10.2.2);
3941 the VWD shall process the RequestTunnel command. If successfully processed, the VWD is
3942 operating in ‘Virtual WAN mode’ and shall send a RequestTunnelResponse command in
3943 response;
3944 if the TunnelStatus value in the RequestTunnelResponse command is 0x00 (‘Success’), the
3945 CHF is operating in ‘Virtual WAN mode’;
3946 if the VWD is a Type 2 Device that has Virtual WAN capability, the VWD shall close the tunnel
3947 with the TunnelID associated with ProtocolID 6;
3948 if the VWD is a PPMID that has Virtual WAN capability, the VWD shall keep the tunnel with
3949 the TunnelID associated with ProtocolID 6 open but shall restrict the payload of a
