3951 HAN Only Messages sent between PPMID and GSME;
3952 Remote Party Commands destined for the PPMID; and
3953 Remote Party Responses and Alerts originating from the PPMID.
3954 VWD and CHF – establishing communications by Remote Party
3955 The Remote Party shall send a CCS01 Command to the Virtual WAN CH to add the VWD as a
3956 PPMID or Type 2 Device. For clarity, the VWD shall behave as the Device type it is added as.
3957 For the VWD and CHF to operate in ‘Virtual WAN mode’, an ‘Enable Virtual WAN Device’
3958 Command is sent to the CHF. The format of this Command and how it is processed is not
3959 described in this document.
3960 If the ‘Enable Virtual WAN Device’ Command is successfully processed:
3961 1. the CHF shall send a RequestTunnel command to the identified VWD using a
3962 ProtocolID of 0 (as per Section 10.2.2);
Page 201

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3963 the VWD shall process the RequestTunnel command. If successfully processed, the VWD is
3964 operating in ‘Virtual WAN mode’ and shall send a RequestTunnelResponse command in
3965 response; and
3966 if the TunnelStatus value in the RequestTunnelResponse command is 0x00 (‘Success’) the
3967 CHF is operating in ‘Virtual WAN mode’.
3968 VWD and CHF – WAN operation
3969 Whilst the VWD is in the CHF’s Device Log and joined to the SMHAN, and the CHF is
3970 operating in ‘Virtual WAN mode’, any Responses or Alerts received by the CHF from any
3971 SMHAN Device shall be processed according to which WAN Communications Link is active
3972 (as defined in Section 10.9.3.2) as follows:
3973 if the WAN Communications Link is active, the Response or Alert shall be sent to the WAN
3974 Communications Link; or
3975 if the Virtual WAN Communications Link is active, the Response or Alert shall be sent to the
3976 Virtual WAN Communications Link using the TransferData command with the TunnelID
3977 associated with ProtocolID 0.
3978 Downloading firmware images to Devices
3979 Requirements and statements in this Section 11, and in Use Cases ‘CS05b Distribute
3980 Firmware to ESME / GSME’ and ‘CS06 Activate Firmware’, shall apply to an SAPC as if it were
3981 an ESME.
3982 Introduction – informative
3983 Compared to other Smart Metering messages, firmware images are large. Further, each
3984 image is likely to be applicable to a significant number of Devices. Thus, an end-to-end,
3985 unicast Message to each affected Device, with each message containing a copy of the image,
3986 is not efficient from a WAN perspective.
3987 This leads to the firmware update process being separated into two stages for ESME, GSME,
3988 HCALCS and Communications Hubs:
3989 distribution of the image to end Devices without any activation of that image; and
3990 a separate and subsequent ‘activation’ Command to each Device.
3991 The Distribute Firmware Command is not a Critical Command (since it does not affect the
3992 operating firmware) and does not need to be unicast.
3993 The Activate Firmware Command is a Critical Command and so must be unicast – as it must
3994 be digitally signed and be for one, and only one specified Device. Further, the Activate
3995 Command must apply to one, and only one, image and that image must have originated
Page 202

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
3996 from the same party that signs the Activate Firmware Command (that is, the party
3997 responsible for that Device). To meet these requirements:
3998 the Activate Firmware Command is of type SME.C.C and so the Signature and MAC on the
3999 Command shall have been verified by the Device prior to the Hash validation (see next
4000 bullet); and
4001 a Device receiving an Activate Firmware Command shall calculate a Hash over the
4002 Manufacturer Image it holds and ensure the Hash so calculated matches that in the Activate
4003 Firmware Command, before the Device attempts to activate the corresponding
4004 Manufacturer Image.
4005 For PPMID the firmware image is delivered to the Communications Hub and transferred to
4006 the target Device. Upon successful transfer of the firmware image the Communications Hub
4007 instructs the PPMID to activate the firmware image.
4008 The GBCS does not constrain the mechanisms used by Device manufacturers to ensure that
4009 only valid Manufacturer Images are activated on Devices manufactured by them. The GBCS
4010 does require that the manufacturer information related to a Manufacturer Image is made
4011 available, so that the Upgrade Image and the ZigBee Over-The-Air (OTA) Header can be
4012 provided when requesting distribution of an image.
4013 In common with other Messages, the GBCS shall not constrain the mechanisms by which the
4014 firmware Messages are transported to the Communications Hub. The GBCS constrains HAN
4015 transport mechanisms to those provided by ZSE.
4016 In line with the ZigBee OTA specification at section 5.1, the contents of Manufacturer Images
4017 sent to Devices are manufacturer defined. Thus, a particular Manufacturer Image may
4018 consist of whatever the manufacturer requires to achieve the necessary update which could
4019 be a full image or just a patch to application code or any other manufacturer specified
4020 content.
4021 Therefore the steps taken by a Device when it activates the contents of a particular
4022 Manufacturer Image are manufacturer specific and specified in the release note for that
4023 Manufacturer Image. Thus, activation of a Manufacturer Image means the set of
4024 manufacturer specified steps the Device takes in processing the content of the image and
4025 terms such as ‘activation’, ‘activate’, ‘activated’, ‘installed’ etc. in the GBCS and the Technical
4026 Specifications, are meant in this sense.
4027 Therefore, when a Device reports its ‘installed’ or ‘active’ firmware version it shall respond
4028 with either:
Page 203

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
4029 the firmware version for its mostly recently successfully activated Manufacturer Image (with
4030 the value in the corresponding OTA Header and so the value in the Central Products List
4031 (CPL) with its SEC meaning); or
4032 if it has never successfully activated a new Manufacturer Image, the firmware version it held
4033 on installation (which again would correspond to the CPL).

4091 Construction of Upgrade Image
4092 For an ESME, GSME or HCALCS firmware image, the Authorising Remote Party shall be the
4093 Supplier for the target Device.
4094 For a Communications Hub firmware image, the Authorising Remote Party shall be the WAN
4095 Provider for the target Device.

4097 concatenation:
4098 Manufacturer Image || Force Replace || 0x40 || Authorising Remote Party Signature
4099 where:
4100 Manufacturer Image shall contain the firmware image the Device is to apply and any
4101 manufacturer specific data needed. For clarity, the GBCS shall not constrain the structure or
4102 contents of Manufacturer Image;
4103 Force Replace shall be a single octet where Force Replace = 0x00 shall mean do not force the
4104 replacement of the currently stored image; and
4105 Authorising Remote Party Signature shall be calculated across the Manufacturer Image using
4106 the Authorising Remote Party’s Private Digital Signing Key.
4107 For a PPMID firmware image, the Upgrade Image shall be the Manufacturer Image where:
4108 Manufacturer Image shall contain the firmware image the PPMID is to apply and any

4110 contents of the PPMID Manufacturer Image.
4111

4117  Table 11.2.3:  Population of the OTA Header
4118  The OTA Header shall uniquely identify a firmware image.
4119  Construction of Manufacturer Image Hash
4120  Manufacturer Image Hash shall be a Hash calculated across the whole Manufacturer Image
4121  file that is provided to the Authorising Remote Party or the Remote Party in case of the
4122  PPMID.
4123  Verification of the authenticity of the Upgrade Image
4124  The Device shall verify Upgrade Image by verifying the Authorising Remote Party Signature
4125  using Manufacturer Image and the Authorising Remote Party’s Public Key.  For clarity, this
4126  shall be the only ECDSA verification required by the GBCS and this is not the ZSE ECDSA
4127  Signature sub-element.
|     |     |     | Page 207  |
| --- | --- | --- | --------- |

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
4128 For an ESME, GSME or HCALCS receiving an Upgrade Image, the Authorising Remote Party’s
4129 Public Key shall be that held by the Device in the {supplier, digitalSignature, management}
4130 Trust Anchor Cell.
4131 For a Communications Hub receiving an Upgrade Image, the Authorising Remote Party’s
4132 Public Key shall be that held by the Device in the {wanProvider, digitalSignature,
4133 management} Trust Anchor Cell.
4134 For a PPMID receiving an Upgrade Image the verification of the authenticity of the Upgrade
4135 Image in this section shall not apply.
4136
4137 Construction of Firmware Distribution Receipt Alert
4138 If the Device is an ESME or HCALCS, the ‘Alert Payload’ fields shall be populated according to
4139 Section 7.2.9.
4140 If the Device is a GSME, the ‘Alert Payload’ fields shall be populated according to Section
4141 7.2.10.
4142 In the above cases, the Device shall:
4143 populate the Use Case Specific Additional Content with the concatenation
4144 0x0920 || the calculated Manufacturer Image Hash
4145 populate the Alert Code field with 0x8F1C (failure), or 0x8F72 (success).
4146 If the Device is a PPMID, no Firmware Distribution Alert shall be sent.
4147
4148 Activation of firmware images
4149 The Activate Firmware Command shall be of type SME.C.C.
4150 A Device other than the PPMID receiving such a Command shall undertake the verifications
4151 required of a SME.C.C Command.
4152 If all such SME.C.C verifications succeed, the Device shall then calculate Manufacturer Image
4153 Hash over the Manufacturer Image it holds and compare that with the Manufacturer Image
4154 Hash specified in the Activate Firmware Command (see Use Case CS06 in Section 11.5 for
4155 details of the Activate Firmware Command Payload construction).
4156 If the two Hashes match, the Device shall attempt to activate the firmware image.
4157 If the two Hashes do not match, the Device shall not attempt to activate the firmware image.
Page 208

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
4158 The Device shall issue a relevant Activate Firmware Response detailing the success or failure
4159 (see Use Case CS06 in Section 11.5 for details of the Activate Firmware Command Payload
4160 construction).
4161 See Section 11.6 for the activation of Upgrade Images for the PPMID.

4185 ESME, GSME and HCALCS shall use the ZCL Image Block Request and Image Block Response
4186 commands to retrieve available OTA images.
4187 ESME, GSME and HCALCS shall not use the ZCL Query Specific File Request and Query Specific
4188 File Response commands.
4189 The OTA Upgrade Image shall be populated according to Section 11.2.3.
4190 The OTA Upgrade Image shall be transported to the Communications Hub through which the
4191 Device communicates.
4192 The Communications Hub shall update its OTA Cluster to reflect availability of the OTA
4193 Upgrade Image, once the image is received by the Communications Hub.
4194 The Communications Hub, as OTA Server, shall indicate availability of an OTA Upgrade Image
4195 differently for ESME, HCALCS and GSME:
4196 for ESME and HCALCS, the Communications Hub shall send a Image Notify command; and
4197 for GSME, the Communications Hub shall set a the New OTA Firmware flag (Bit Number 0) in
4198 FunctionalNotificationFlags.
4199 For each ESME / GSME / HCALCS Device Entity Identifier associated with the OTA Upgrade
4200 Image, the Communications Hub shall
4201 1. verify whether the ESME / GSME / HCALCS Hardware Version is present in the Query
4202 Next Image Request Command;
4203 1. if the Hardware Version is present and does not fall between the minimum and
4204 maximum Hardware Version in the OTA Header the Communications Hub shall set
4205 transferResponseCode to hardwareVersionMismatch as specified in
4206 Section 11.7 and process from step 5;
Page 211

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
4207 2. if the Hardware Version is not present, or is present and falls between the minimum
4208 and maximum Hardware Version in the OTA Header, the Communications Hub shall
4209 make the OTA Upgrade Image available to the ESME / GSME / HCALCS in the Query
4210 Next Image Response Command;
4211 3. The ESME / GSME / HCALCS shall download an OTA Upgrade Image when it is aware
4212 of the availability of a suitable OTA Upgrade Image using the QueryNextImage and
4213 Image Block/Page commands specified in the OTA Cluster specification27;
4214 4. upon the reception of the Upgrade End Request Command from the ESME / GSME /
4215 HCALCS, the Communications Hub shall;
4216 1. set transferResponseCode to fileTransferSuccess if the transfer of
4217 the OTA Upgrade Image has completed successfully and process from step 4;
4218 2. set transferResponseCode to fileTransferFailure if the transfer of
4219 the OTA Upgrade Image has failed, and process from step 5;
4220 3. the Communications Hub shall create an Alert with the Alert Code field set to 0x8F8A
4221 as specified in Section 11.7, set firmwareVersion to the OTA Upgrade Image File
4222 version, include the transferResponseCode from the previous step and
4223 process from step 6;
4224 4. the Communications Hub shall create an Alert with the Alert Code field set to 0x8F89
4225 as specified in Section 11.7, set firmwareVersion to the OTA Upgrade Image File
4226 version, include the transferResponseCode from the previous step and
4227 process from step 6;
4228 5. the Communications Hub shall send the Alert created in the previous step.
4229 The ESME / GSME / HCALCS shall verify the Upgrade Image contained within the OTA
4230 Upgrade Image according to Section 11.2.5, and the ESME / GSME shall update its Event Log
4231 with the outcome of that verification.
4232 If the verification is successful, the ESME / GSME / HCALCS shall construct and send a
4233 Firmware Distribution Receipt Alert, according to Section 11.2.6, and shall store the
4234 Manufacturer Image contained within the OTA Upgrade Image.
4235 If the verification is not successful, the Device shall discard the OTA Upgrade Image, and
4236 send a Firmware Distribution Receipt Alert, as detailed in Section 11.2.6.
4237 On receipt of a Firmware Distribution Receipt Alert, the Supplier may verify the
4238 cryptographic protection as specified in Section 6.7.3.

4255 Device processing of Command and Response handling
4256 The Device receiving an Activate Firmware Command shall undertake processing steps in the
4257 sequence defined in this Section 11.5.2.2.
Page 214

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
4258 The Device shall:
4259 1. undertake Command Authenticity and Integrity Verification as required for a Command
4260 of the SME.C.C Message Category;
4261 2. if executionDateTime is present then the Device shall:
4262 record manufacturerImageHash, originatorCounter and executionDateTime;
4263 construct and send a Response where executionOutcome is not present. Grouping Header is
4264 constructed and Response Cryptographic Protection is applied as required for a Response of
4265 the SME.C.C Message Categories; and
4266 at the date-time specified in executionDateTime, or immediately if the executionDateTime is
4267 in the past, undertake the processing from step 3.
4268 If executionDateTime is not present then the Device shall continue processing from step
4269 3 immediately;
4270 3. if the Device does not have a stored Manufacturer Image then set
4271 activateImageResponseCode to noImageHeld and process from step 7;
4272 4. calculate Manufacturer Image Hash. If the calculated value does not equal
4273 manufacturerImageHash then the Device shall set
4274 activateImageResponseCode to hashMismatch and process from step 7;
4275 5. attempt to activate Manufacturer Image. If the activate fails then the Device shall set
4276 activateImageResponseCode to activationFailure and process from
4277 step 7;
4278 6. set activateImageResponseCode to success;
4279 7. populate the executionOutcome according to the requirements of Section 11.5.2.3 using
4280 the activateImageResponseCode value produced by the processing in this
4281 Section 11.5.2.2, the value of originatorCounter from the Command and the
4282 version of firmware now in operation to populate firmwareVersion;
4283 8. construct Grouping Header and apply the Response Cryptographic Protection required
4284 for a Response / Alert of the SME.C.C / SME.A.C Message Categories respectively. In
4285 such an Alert, the Message Code shall be 0x00CA. The Response / Alert shall be
4286 addressed to the Business Originator of the Corresponding Command. If
4287 activateImageResponseCode is success then alertCode shall be 0x8F66
4288 else alertCode shall be 0x8F67; and
4289 9. send the Response if executionDateTime was not present in the Command or send
4290 the Alert if executionDateTime was present in the Command.

4580  contain the authorityKeyIdentifier extension, except where the Security Credential
| 4581  | Document is self-signed;  |     |     |
| ----- | ------------------------- | --- | --- |

| ----- | ---------------- | --- | --- |

4586  public keys shall be elliptic curve public keys on the NIST P-256 curve;

4588  uncompressed form as detailed in section 2.2 of IETF RFC 548030;

4702 Device Security Credentials – informative
Page 231

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
4703 In terms of processing relating to a Device’s own Security Credentials:
4704 the Command to Devices for issuing Device Certification Requests (and therefore generate
4705 new Public-Private Key Pairs) is covered in Section 13.4;
4706 the Command to Devices for the Device to replace a current Device Certificate with a new
4707 Device Certificate resulting from a Device Certification Request is covered in Section 13.5, as
4708 are the related requirements for the capability to store such Certificates; and
4709 the Command to a Device to provide a copy of its currently held Device Certificates is
4710 covered Section 13.6.
4711 Remote Party Security Credentials – informative
4712 This Section 13.1.2 summarises the GBCS requirements in relation to storing, replacing and
4713 providing details of Remote Party Security Credentials. The use of such credentials to
4714 control access to Device functions is detailed in other Sections of the GBCS and in relevant
4715 Use Cases.
4716 A Remote Party Security Credential is a Public Key Certificate which securely binds together
4717 the Remote Party’s identity with a Public Key along with related information, including what
4718 that Public Key can be used for and over what time period it is valid. The corresponding
4719 Private Key should be securely controlled solely by the Remote Party and known only to that
4720 Remote Party.
4721 The purpose of storing each Remote Party Public Key (and related details) on a Device is so
4722 that each Public Key can act as a ‘Trust Anchor’ for the Device. The Device uses these Trust
4723 Anchors to check cryptographically whether Remote Party Messages can be trusted or not
4724 (and so whether it should act on them or not). Thus, all of a Device’s Trust Anchors must be
4725 populated.
4726 Trust Anchors need to be capable of being replaced during a Device’s operational life for a
4727 number of reasons including:
4728 the Certificate’s expiry (Organisation Certificates will only be valid for a fixed period of time);
4729 the Known Party transferring control to a different organisation (for example on Change of
4730 Supplier);
4731 the cryptographic algorithms, or parameters such as key length, needing to be changed;
4732 the Known Party having lost the use of the corresponding Private Key; or
4733 there being concerns that someone other than the Known Party has use of, or may have use
4734 of, the corresponding Private Key.
Page 232

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
4735 Thus, an ‘Update Security Credentials Command’ must be supported by all Devices that rely
4736 on Remote Party Security Credentials to act as Trust Anchors. Related, all such Devices need
4737 to support a ‘Provide Security Credential Details’ Command, so that Remote Parties can be
4738 sure which Devices need to have credentials replaced.
4739 However, if these Trust Anchors could be replaced without proper protections, attackers
4740 could take over control of Devices or the Devices could be rendered inoperable. Thus, a
4741 Device needs to do thorough checks before applying an Update Security Credentials
4742 Command. The checks that the Device can and must do vary dependent on the reasons for
4743 the change. Thus, Section 13.2.1 lays out a number of different checks and the
4744 circumstances in which corresponding Commands may be issued. Broadly the following
4745 checks are carried out by the Device:
4746 is the Command properly formed?
4747 is the Command for the Device that it has been delivered to, and is the Command one that it
4748 has not processed previously?
4749 are the Remote Parties apparently authorising the Command allowed to authorise it?
4750 was the Command Authorised by the Remote Parties that it appears to be Authorised by?
4751 were the Certificates in the payload of the Command issued by properly Authorised parties,
4752 specifically by Certification Authorities Authorised (by ‘root’ under the APKI) to issue GB
4753 Smart Metering Certificates?
4754 Only when a Device has successfully undertaken all five sets of checks should it action the
4755 Update Security Credentials Command.
4756 Other Critical Commands only have to complete the first four categories of check.
4757 Trust Anchor Management Protocol (TAMP) – informative
4758 The GBCS does not specify a fully compliant TAMP solution due to the limited processing and
4759 networking capability of Devices. However, it does incorporate checks that are functionally
4760 derived from relevant checks in IETF RFC 5934.
4761 The GBCS only permits a restricted subset of ‘IETF RFC 5934 like’ functionality:
4762 replacement of Trust Anchors is required (and specified in this Use Case) but their addition,
4763 change or removal is not allowed;
4764 status queries are supported (and are specified in this Section 13.1.3); and
4765 community related functions are not supported.

4779 The ‘CS02a Provide Security Credential Details’ Command and Response
4780 This Section 13.2.3.2 summarises the structure of the CS02a Provide Security Credential Details Command.
4781 If protected by an Access Control Broker MAC as per Section 13.2.4.2, a CS02a Provide Security Credential Details Command shall be the
4782 concatenation:
4783 MAC Header || Grouping Header || @ProvideSecurityCredentialDetails.Command || 0x00 || ACB-SMD MAC
4784 If protected by a KRP Signature as per Section 13.2.4.2, a CS02a Provide Security Credential Details Command shall be the concatenation:
4785 Grouping Header || @ProvideSecurityCredentialDetails.Command || 0x40 || KRP Signature
4786 If an SMD Signature is required as per Section 13.2.4.5, a CS02a Provide Security Credential Details Response shall be the concatenation:
4787 Grouping Header || @ProvideSecurityCredentialDetails.Response || 0x40 || SMD Signature
4788 If an SMD Signature is not required as per Section 13.2.4.5, a CS02a Provide Security Credential Details Response shall be the concatenation:
4789 MAC Header || Grouping Header || @ProvideSecurityCredentialDetails.Response || 0x00 || SMD-KRP MAC
4790 Where:
4791 @ProvideSecurityCredentialDetails.Command and Response shall each be an octet string containing the DER encoding of the populated ASN.1
4792 structure (as laid out in Section 13.2.3.3);
4793 0x40 is the length in octets of Signature when a SMD or KRP Signature is present, and 0x00 is the length in octets of Signature when a SMD or
4794 KRP Signature is not present;
4795 KRP Signature and ACB-SMD MAC are as defined in Section 13.2.4.2;
4796 SMD Signature and SMD-KRP MAC are as defined in Section 13.2.4.5; and
Page 236

5020 Command, Response and Alert Structure
5021 The Update Security Credentials Command
5022 This Section 13.3.3.1 summarises the structure of the Update Security Credentials Command, which depends on credentialsReplacementMode
5023 and the deviceType of the Device.
5024 If credentialsReplacementMode = anyByContingency or anyExceptAbnormalRootByRecovery then an Update Security Credential Details
5025 Command shall be the concatenation:
Page 258

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5026 Grouping Header || @UpdateSecurityCredentials.CommandPayload || 0x40 || KRP Signature
5027 If credentialsReplacementMode = accessControlBrokerByACB and deviceType is not
5028 communicationsHubCommunicationsHubFunction then an Update Security Credentials Command shall be the concatenation:
5029 MAC Header || Grouping Header || @UpdateSecurityCredentials.CommandPayload || 0x00 || ACB-SMD MAC
5030 In all other cases, the Update Security Credentials Command shall be the concatenation:
5031 MAC Header || Grouping Header || @UpdateSecurityCredentials.CommandPayload || 0x40 || KRP Signature|| ACB-SMD MAC
5032 In these Command structures:
5033 @UpdateSecurityCredentials.CommandPayload shall be an octet string containing the DER encoding of the populated ASN.1 structure (as laid
5034 out in Section 13.3.5.11);
5035 Grouping Header shall be constructed as specified in Section 7.2.7 with Business Originator ID being the Entity Identifier of the Known Remote
5036 Party which generated KRP Signature, and with Business Originator Counter being that of the same Known Remote Party;
5037 KRP Signature shall be generated as specified in Section 6.3.3;
5038 ACB Grouping Header shall be constructed as specified in Section 7.2.7 with Business Originator ID being the Entity Identifier of the Access
5039 Control Broker and Business Originator Counter being that of the Access Control Broker;
5040 MAC Header shall be constructed as specified in Section 7.2.5; and
5041 ACB-SMD MAC shall be calculated as specified in Section 6.2.3.
5042 The Update Security Credentials Response
5043 An Update Security Credentials Response shall be the concatenation:
Page 259

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5044 Grouping Header || @UpdateSecurityCredentials.ResponsePayload || 0x40 || SMD Signature
5045 where:
5046 @UpdateSecurityCredentials.ResponsePayload shall be an octet string containing the DER encoding of the populated ASN.1 structure (as laid
5047 out in Section 13.3.5.11);
5048 Grouping Header in the Response shall be constructed as specified in Section 7.2.7 with Business Target ID being the Entity Identifier specified
5049 in the corresponding Command’s Grouping Header; and
5050 SMD Signature shall be generated as specified in Section 6.3.5.
5051 The Update Security Credentials Alert
5052 An Update Security Credentials Alert shall be the concatenation:
5053 Grouping Header || @UpdateSecurityCredentials.AlertPayload || 0x40 || SMD Signature
5054 where:
5055 @UpdateSecurityCredentials.AlertPayload shall be an octet string containing the DER encoding of the populated ASN.1 structure (as laid out in
5056 Section 13.3.5.11);
5057 Grouping Header in the Alert shall be constructed as specified in Section 7.2.7 with Business Target ID being the Entity Identifier specified in the
5058 corresponding Command’s Grouping Header;
5059 the Message Code being 0x00CB; and
5060 2. SMD Signature shall be generated as specified in Section 6.3.5.
5061 The Update Security Credentials Command, Response and Alert – informative
Page 260

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5062 The @UpdateSecurityCredentials.CommandPayload structure has four parts:
5063 authorisingRemotePartyControl: which includes details of what kind of credential replacement this Command is, which Remote Parties are
5064 authorising it and information to support Protection Against Replay protections;
5065 replacements: which is a list of new Certificates the Device is to store details from, along with which Trust Anchor Cell each set of details is to
5066 be stored in on the Device;
5067 certificationPathCertificates: which is a list of Certification Authority Certificates the Device will need to use in checking that the replacement
5068 Certificates were properly issued; and
5069 executionDateTime: which, if present, specifies the date-time at which the certificates in the CommandPayload are to be used to replace the
5070 credentials currently in use on the Device. If this field is not present, the Command shall be executed immediately. If this field has the value
5071 equivalent to ‘never’ (which is '99991231235959Z') the certificate replacement will never happen. This is to allow cancellation of future dated
5072 Commands. Note that future dating is not supported where certificates are being replaced in exception conditions.
5073 The @UpdateSecurityCredentials.Response structure contains, for immediate execution commands, a list detailing the success of failure of
5074 each of the replacements, including details of the parties affected. For future dated commands, @UpdateSecurityCredentials.AlertPayload
5075 structure contains the list detailing the success, or failure, of each of the replacements, including details of the parties affected.
5076 Section 13.3.5.11 contains narrative for each of the parts of these ASN.1 structures.
5077 Section 18.3.1 provides an illustrative instantiation of @UpdateSecurityCredentials.CommandPayload and its corresponding DER encoding.
5078 Updating Security Credentials on a Device – Processing Steps
5079 This Section lays out the requirements for the construction, protection and Authentication of the Update Security Credentials Command
5080 Payload, the processing required on the Device of the Command, the construction of the corresponding Response Payload and, where required,
5081 the Alert Payload.

5085  Table 13.3.4.1:  Attribute values for Update Security Credentials Command
5086  Command Authenticity and Integrity Verification
5087  The Device shall undertake processing according to the requirements of Section 13.3.5.1.
5088  Should any of the checks detailed in Section 13.3.5.1 fail then the Device shall:
5089  generate an entry in the Security Log recording failed Authentication;
5090  discard the Command without execution and without sending a Response; and
|     |     |     |     | Page 271  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --------- |

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5091 send an Alert notifying the failed Authentication, constructed as specified in Section 6.2.4.2 of the GBCS, populated with the relevant Alert
5092 Code according to Section 16, to the Known Remote Party identified by:
5093 the Trust Anchor Cell {supplier, digitalSignature, management} if the Device’s deviceType is not
5094 communicationsHubCommunicationsHubFunction; or
5095 the Trust Anchor Cell {wanProvider, digitalSignature, management} if the Device’s deviceType is
5096 communicationsHubCommunicationsHubFunction.
5097 Where all of the checks detailed in Section 13.3.5.1 succeed the Device shall process the Command and produce a Response.
5098 Command Processing
5099 Before undertaking any further processing, the Device shall update Execution Counter to the value of authorisingRemotePartySeqNumber.
5100 If executionDateTime is present then the Device shall:
5101 record against the remotePartyRole (as specified in authorisingRemotePartyControl ), authorisingRemotePartyControl, replacements; and
5102 executionDateTime;
5103 construct a Response where executionOutcome is not present according to the requirements of Section 13.3.4.4; and
5104 at the date-time specified in executionDateTime, or immediately if the executionDateTime is in the past undertake the processing of Section
5105 13.3.4.3.1 then construct an Alert according to the requirements of Section 13.3.4.5.
5106 If executionDateTime is not present then the Device shall:
5107 undertake the processing of Section 13.3.4.3.1; and
5108 construct a Response where executionOutcome is present according to the requirements of Section 13.3.4.4.
5109 replacements Processing
Page 272

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5110 For each of the targetTrustAnchorCell in replacements, the Device shall:
5111 record the entityIdentifier and subjectKeyIdentifier currently held in that targetTrustAnchorCell;
5112 attempt to replace the contents of that targetTrustAnchorCell using the corresponding certificate in TrustAnchorReplacement; and
5113 if the contents of the replacement are successfully applied, undertake the processing required by Section 13.3.5.10 in relation to the
5114 RemotePartyRole for that targetTrustAnchorCell.
5115 For clarity, before the contents of a certificate are used to replace the contents of a targetTrustAnchorCell, the Device shall have successfully
5116 undertaken the checks in Section 13.3.5.9 in relation to that certificate. Should a check in 13.3.5.9 not succeed then, in line with Section
5117 4.3.2.8.2, the Device shall undertake no further processing of the Command, except for the issuance of a Message containing an
5118 executionOutcome.
5119 Response Construction
5120 The @UpdateSecurityCredentials.ResponsePayload shall have the structure defined in Section 13.3.5.11, and the Device shall populate the
5121 executionOutcome, where present with values according to Table 13.3.4.6.
5122 Alert Construction
5123 The @UpdateSecurityCredentials.AlertPayload shall have the structure defined in Section 13.3.4, and the Device shall populate the
5124 executionOutcome, with values according to Table 13.3.4.6.

5134 Preventing Replay of Commands
5135 The Protection Against Replay mechanisms for the Update Security Credentials Command shall be that specified in this Section 13.3.5.3 (which
5136 is different than that for other GBCS Commands).
5137 For each of RemotePartyRole from which the Device can receive a valid Updated Security Credentials Command, the Device shall allocate
5138 storage for an Execution Counter which shall be capable of storing a 64 bit unsigned integer and which shall initially be set to the value zero at
5139 manufacture. For transitionalCoS, the Device may allocate storage for an additional Execution Counter, credentialsReplacementModes.
5140 Before executing any Update Security Credentials Command, a Device shall confirm that, if CredentialsReplacementMode <>
5141 accessControlBrokerByACB, then
5142 (authorisingRemotePartyTACellIdentifier is populated in the Command) and (the authorisingRemotePartySeqNumber is strictly numerically
5143 greater than the Execution Counter the Device has recorded for the RemotePartyRole identified in authorisingRemotePartyTACellIdentifier and,
5144 where relevant for transitionalCoS, the credentialsReplacementMode);
5145 else
Page 282

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5146 (the authorisingRemotePartySeqNumber is strictly numerically greater than the Execution Counter the Device has recorded for the
5147 accessControlBroker).
5148 Required Trust Anchor Cells by Device Type
5149 The Trust Anchor Cells specified in Section 4.3.2.5 are those required on each Device type and so are the only valid targetTrustAnchorCells.
5150 The Device shall ensure that all targetTrustAnchorCells specified in the Command instance are valid for the type of Device it is, according to the
5151 requirements of Section 4.3.2.5. A Command containing any invalid targetTrustAnchorCells shall not be processed any further by the Device.

5182 Verifying the CryptographicProtections
5183 In verifying Cryptographic Protections pursuant to this Section 13.3.5.8:
5184 KRP Signature shall, where required by Section 13.3.3.1 for the specified Message Code and credentialsReplacementMode, be verified
5185 according to the requirements in this Section 13.3.5.8; and
5186 ACB-SMD MAC, where required by Section 13.3.3.1 for the specified Message Code and credentialsReplacementMode, shall be verified
5187 according to the requirements in Section 6.2.4.1.2.
5188 If credentialsReplacementMode = anyByContingency or Message Code = 0x0109 then KRP Signature shall be verified using the public key
5189 established according to the requirements of Section 13.3.5.8.1.
5190 If credentialsReplacementMode = <> anyByContingency or Message Code =<> 0x0109 then KRP Signature shall be verified using the public key
5191 identified as per Section 4.3.2.7.2.
Page 286

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5192 If credentialsReplacementMode = accessControlBrokerByACB or Message Code = 0x0104 and deviceType is not
5193 communicationsHubCommunicationsHubFunction then ACB-SMD MAC shall be verified as per Section 6.2.4.1.2.
5194 Decrypting the contingency public key and verifying Authorising Remote Party’s digital signature against that decrypted key
5195 The Device shall decrypt the Contingency Key that it holds in Trust Anchor Cell {root, keyCertSign, management} by undertaking Decryption
5196 using the following parameters:
5197 setting Ciphertext to be encrypted value of the Contingency Key;
5198 setting Additional Authenticated Data to be 0x31;
5199 setting the Initialization Vector to be 0xFFFFFFFF0000000000000000; and
5200 setting the shared symmetric key to be the value in plaintextSymmetricKey.
5201 Where Decryption is successful, the Device shall use the Plaintext produced as the Public Key to verify KRP Signature according to the
5202 requirements at Section 6.3.4.
5203 The Contingency Key shall have been Encrypted accordingly.
5204 Verifying the authenticity of replacement certificates
5205 For each replacementCertificate in replacements, the Device shall first apply the requirements of Section 12.6 (Device processing
5206 of Certificates). If any of those checks fail, the Section 13.3.5.9 check fails.
5207 Where Certification Path Validation is required by this Section 13.3.5.9, the application of time based checks shall be determined as follows:
5208 if, in the Command, applyTimeBasedCPVChecks = disapply then time based checks shall NOT be applied by the Device; and
5209 otherwise time based checks shall be applied or not applied in line with the requirements of Section 4.3.2.8.

5224 Validation of new root Certificate against current root Security Credentials
5225 The Device shall:
5226 identify the Certificate in replacements that corresponds to the targetTrustAnchorCell of {root, keyCertSign, management}. The Certificate shall
5227 be referred to as NewWithNew; then
5228 identify the Certificate in certificationPathCertificates that has the same subjectPublicKey as the NewWithNew Certificate and where
5229 RemotePartyRole in the X520OrganisationalUnitName field = root. The Certificate shall be referred to as NewWithOld. If no such Certificate is
5230 found, the Section 13.3.5.9.1 check fails else:
Page 288

5231 use the Public Key in the {root, keyCertSign, management} Trust Anchor Cell to verify the digital signature in NewWithOld. If the digital
5232 signature verification fails, the Section 13.3.5.9.1 check fails else:
5233 use the Public Key in NewWithNew to verify the digital signature in NewWithNew. If the digital signature verification fails, the Section
5234 13.3.5.9.1 check fails.

5290 The @UpdateSecurityCredentials.CommandPayload,@UpdateSecurityCredentials.ResponsePayload and
5291 @UpdateSecurityCredentials.AlertPayload structure definition
5292 Each instance of @UpdateSecurityCredentials.CommandPayload, @UpdateSecurityCredentials.ResponsePayload and of
5293 @UpdateSecurityCredentials.AlertPayload shall be an octet string containing the DER encoding of the populated structure defined in this
5294 Section 13.3.4, which specifies the structure in ASN.1.
5295 The structure of Certificate shall be as defined in ASN.1 in IETF RFC 5912. Note that the Certificate structures within IETF RFC 5912 begin
5296 after the phrase ‘Certificate- and CRL-specific structures begin here’.

5304 -- in control.
5305 -- The Remote Party authorising the Command is that party which generated the KRP Signature (or the Access Control Broker
5306 -- if there is no KRP Signature)

5596 Requirements for AuthorisingRemotePartyControl elements – informative
5597 All bar two parts of the AuthorisingRemotePartyControl structure are optional. This Section summarises when each of the optional elements
5598 needs to be present.
AuthorisingRemotePartyControl element Notes
credentialsReplacementMode Always required
plaintextSymmetricKey Only required if credentialsReplacementMode = anyByContingency (when it is always
required)
applyTimeBasedCPVChecks Only required if the Device is to ignore time when undertaking Certification Path
Validation, in which case it needs to have the value ‘disapply’
authorisingRemotePartyTACellIdentifier For a Communications Hub, always present.
For all other Devices, always present unless the Access Control Broker is replacing its
own Key Agreement credentials (in which case it should be omitted)
authorisingRemotePartySeqNumber Always required
newRemotePartyFloorSeqNumber If the Command is to effect a change of control, then
newRemotePartyFloorSeqNumber should be included. It can be present in all other
situations
newRemotePartySpecialistFloorSeqNumber Only required on Change of Supplier where the new Supplier has decided to use a
different sequence of Originator Counters for Prepayment Top Ups.
otherRemotePartySeqNumberChanges Should be present if one role (e.g. recovery, transitionalCoS) is changing credentials for
Page 310

AuthorisingRemotePartyControl element Notes
another role or roles (e.g. supplier). In such cases, this should be present to set

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5611 Device processing of Commands and Response handling
5612 The Device receiving an Issue Security Credentials Command shall undertake processing
5613 steps in the sequence defined in this Section 13.4.4.
5614 In processing an Issue Security Credentials Command, the Device shall:
5615 1. undertake Command Authenticity and Integrity Verification as required for a Command
5616 of Message Category SME.C.C. The Security Credentials used to verify Cryptographic
5617 Protection I shall be:
5618 those held in the {wANProvider, digitalSignature, management} Trust Anchor Cell, if the
5619 target Device’s deviceType equals communicationsHubCommunicationsHubFunction;
5620 those held in the {supplier, digitalSignature, management} Trust Anchor Cell, if the target
5621 Device’s deviceType does not equal communicationsHubCommunicationsHubFunction;
5622 2. validate that the value of keyUsage in CommandPayload is either digitalSignature only
5623 or keyAgreement only. If this validation fails then the Device shall set
5624 issueCredentialsResponseCode to invalidKeyUsage, and process from step 6;
5625 3. generate a Private-Public Key Pair and store the Private Key so generated in the Pending
5626 Private Key Cell determined by the value of keyUsage in CommandPayload. If the step
5627 fails then the Device shall set issueCredentialsResponseCode to keyPairGenerationFailed,
5628 and process from step 6;
5629 4. with the ASN.1 terms in this step (that are not defined in this Section 13.4.4) having the
5630 meaning of IETF RFC 298636; generate a CertificationRequest which:
5631 complies with the requirements of IETF RFC2986 and IETF RFC 5912;
5632 is DER encoded, in line with the recommendation of IETF RFC 596737;
5633 has subjectPublicKey set to the bit string representation of the Public Key generated in step
5634 3;
5635 incorporates an extensionRequest identified by id-ce-keyUsage which shall contain the
5636 keyUsage value specified in CommandPayload;
5637 incorporates an extensionRequest identified by id-ce-subjectAltName which shall contain a
5638 single GeneralName of type OtherName that is further sub-typed as a
36 https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2986
37 https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5967
Page 313

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5639 HardwareModuleName (id-on-HardwareModuleName) as defined in IETF RFC 4108. The
5640 hwSerialNum field shall be set to the Device’s Entity Identifier; and
5641 has the signature generated using the Private Key generated in step 3;
5642 5. if the generation of CertificationRequest is not successful then the Device shall set
5643 issueCredentialsResponseCode to cRProductionFailed; and
5644 6. create a Response according to the requirements of Section 13.4.7, apply the Response
5645 Cryptographic Protection required for a Response of Message Category SME.C.C, and
5646 send the Response.
5647 Response Processing
5648 Response Recipient Verification may be undertaken as specified in this GBCS for a Response
5649 of Message Category SME.C.C. The issueCredentialsResponseCode field, where present in
5650 the Response, may be decoded according to the ASN.1 definitions at Section 13.4.6.

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5719 Device processing of Commands and Response handling
5720 The Device receiving an Update Device Certificate on Device Command shall undertake
5721 processing steps in the sequence defined in this Section 13.5.4.
5722 In processing an Update Device Certificate on Device Command, the Device shall:
5723 1. undertake Command Authenticity and Integrity Verification as required for a Command
5724 of Message Category SME.C.C, except that check 4 in Section 6.2.4.1.1 may be
5725 undertaken after the checks in Section 6.2.4.1.2. The Security Credentials used to verify
5726 Cryptographic Protection I shall be:
5727 those held in the {wANProvider, digitalSignature, management} Trust Anchor Cell, if the
5728 target Device’s deviceType equals communicationsHubCommunicationsHubFunction; or
5729 those held in the {supplier, digitalSignature, management} Trust Anchor Cell, if the target
5730 Device’s deviceType does not equal communicationsHubCommunicationsHubFunction.
5731 2. establish the values of keyUsage, subjectPublicKey and hwSerialNum in certificate in the
5732 CommandPayload. If any of the values cannot be established then the Device shall set
5733 updateDeviceCertResponseCode to invalidCertificate, and process from step 10;
5734 3. validate that hwSerialNum established at step 2 is the Device’s Entity Identifier. If this
5735 validation fails then the Device shall set updateDeviceCertResponseCode to
5736 wrongDeviceIdentity, and process from step 10;
5737 4. validate that keyUsage established at step 2 is either digitalSignature only or
5738 keyAgreement only. If this validation fails then the Device shall set
5739 updateDeviceCertResponseCode to invalidKeyUsage, and process from step 10;
5740 5. validate that the Device holds a Pending Private Key for the keyUsage as established at
5741 step 2. If this validation fails then the Device shall set updateDeviceCertResponseCode
5742 to noCorrespondingKeyPairGenerated, and process from step 10;
5743 6. validate that subjectPublicKey established at step 2 is the bit string representation of the
5744 Public Key corresponding to the Pending Private Key identified at step 5. If this
5745 validation fails then the Device shall set updateDeviceCertResponseCode to
5746 wrongPublicKey, and process from step 10;
5747 7. store certificate. If this step fails then the Device shall set
5748 updateDeviceCertResponseCode to certificateStorageFailed, and process from step 10;
5749 8. set the Current Private Key to have the value of the Pending Private Key for the
5750 keyUsage established at step 2. If this step fails then the Device shall set
5751 updateDeviceCertResponseCode to privateKeyChangeFailed, and process from step 10;
Page 321

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5752 9. set updateDeviceCertResponseCode to success; and
5753 10. create a Response according to the requirements of Section 13.5.7, apply the Response
5754 Cryptographic Protection required for a Response of Message Category SME.C.C, and
5755 send the Response.
5756 If all steps were successful and this was a change of digitalSignature certificate, the
5757 Response shall be signed using the private key corresponding to the new certificate. If there
5758 was a failure, the Response shall be signed using the private key corresponding to the pre-
5759 existing key pair.
5760 Once the Pending Private Key becomes the Current Private Key, the Device will be using the
5761 new Private Key and this will affect all Remote Parties interacting with the Device;
5762 specifically they will need to use the new Certificate corresponding to the Private Key now in
5763 use.
5764 Response Processing
5765 Response Recipient Verification may be undertaken as specified in this GBCS for a Response
5766 of the relevant Message Category. The updateDeviceCertResponseCode field may be
5767 decoded according to the ASN.1 definitions at Section 13.5.6.
5768 If this was a change of digitalSignature certificate, the public key to be used to verify the
5769 Device’s signature is dependent on the value of updateDeviceCertResponseCode. If
5770 updateDeviceCertResponseCode is success then the Private Key used for Signing will
5771 have changed. If updateDeviceCertResponseCode is other than success, the Private
5772 Key used for Signing will not have changed.

5818 Device processing of Commands and Response handling
5819 The Device receiving a Provide Device Certificates from Device Command shall undertake
5820 processing steps in the sequence defined in this Section 13.6.4.
5821 In processing a Provide Device Certificates from Device Command, the Device shall:
5822 1. undertake Command Authenticity and Integrity Verification as required for a Command
5823 of Message Category SME.C.C, except that Cryptographic Protection II shall not be
5824 verified. The Security Credentials used to verify Cryptographic Protection I shall be:
5825 those held in the {wANProvider, digitalSignature, management} Trust Anchor Cell, if the
5826 target Device’s deviceType equals communicationsHubCommunicationsHubFunction; or
5827 those held in the {supplier, digitalSignature, management} Trust Anchor Cell, if the target
5828 Device’s deviceType does not equal communicationsHubCommunicationsHubFunction;
5829 2. validate that keyUsage in CommandPayload is either digitalSignature only or
5830 keyAgreement only. If this validation fails then the Device shall set
5831 provideDeviceCertResponseCode to invalidKeyUsage, and process from step 5;
5832 3. confirm that the Device holds a certificate which (1) is for the keyUsage identified at
5833 step 2, (2) contains in hwSerialNum a value equal to the Device’s Entity Identifier and (3)
5834 contains in subjectPublicKey the bit string representation of the Public Key
5835 corresponding to the Current Private Key for this keyUsage. If this validation fails then
5836 the Device shall set provideDeviceCertResponseCode to noCertificateHeld, and process
5837 from step 5;
5838 4. retrieve the certificate identified in step 3. If this step fails then the Device shall set
5839 provideDeviceCertResponseCode to certificateRetrievalFailure, and process from step 5;
5840 and
5841 5. create a Response according to the requirements of Section 13.6.7, apply the Response
5842 Cryptographic Protection required for a Response of Message Category SME.C.C, and
5843 send the Response.
5844 Response Processing
5845 Response Recipient Verification may be undertaken as specified in this GBCS for a Response
5846 of the Message Category SME.C.C. The provideDeviceCertResponseCode field may be
5847 decoded according to the ASN.1 definitions at Section 13.6.6.

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5906 Pair-wise Authorisation of Devices
5907 Introduction to pair-wise Authorisation of Devices – informative
5908 The role of pair-wise Authorisation – informative
5909 This Section 13.7 includes the Use Cases related to the Authorisation (and the removal of
5910 Authorisation) for pair-wise, secure application layer interaction between two Devices on
5911 the same SMHAN. It also covers the related Use Cases for backing up and restoring the GPF
5912 Device Log.
5913 The process of authorising two Devices to communicate is referred to as ‘Joining’38.
5914 Removal of such authorisation is referred to as ‘Un-joining’. Correspondingly, Remote Party
5915 Commands are specified in this Section 13.7 for instructing Devices that they are to ‘Join’ or
5916 ‘Unjoin’.
5917 In line with the SMETS and CHTS Device Log requirements, two Devices on a HAN must only
5918 be capable of interacting at the application layer if they are currently Joined. They must not
5919 be capable of interacting if (1) they have never been Joined or (2) they have been Unjoined.
5920 The application layer interactions between Devices on the same SMHAN must conform to
5921 the Device Based Access Controls (DBAC) as defined in Section 13.7.3. For example, an
5922 ESME must not be capable of processing an ‘Enable Supply’ Command from an IHD or an
5923 HCALCS.
5924 It is a precondition of Joining that both Devices have been ‘White-listed’ on to the HAN (as
5925 per Use Case ‘CCS01 Add Device to CHF Device log’) so that they are able to communicate
5926 over the HAN at the network layer (and so have network access). The GPF may be
5927 configured to be in the CHF’s Device Log at manufacture. A Device on a white-list can be
5928 removed from the white-list. It must then be unable to communicate over the HAN, and so
5929 unable to interact at the application layer with any Devices to which it was ‘Joined’.
5930 In SMETS terminology:
5931 the CHF’s Device Log holds the list of currently white-listed Devices on the SMHAN; and
5932 the Device Log on an ESME, SAPC, GSME, GPF, HCALCS or PPMID Device holds the Entity
5933 Identifiers, Device Types and related Security Credentials of other Devices on the HAN to
5934 which the Device is currently Joined (and so Authorised to interact with at an application
5935 layer).
5936 The process of white-listing a Device, and its subsequently obtaining network access,
5937 establishes a shared secret key between the Device and the Communications Hub. The Gas
38 This is unrelated to the ZSE meaning of ‘joining’
Page 333

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5938 Proxy Function, which is part of the Communications Hub, uses this shared secret key,
5939 combined with a Device being entered in to its Device Log, for application layer
5940 authorisation.
5941 IHDs and other Type 2 Devices are not required to have a Device Log (as defined in SMETS).
5942 They are required to store security and related details of the Devices to which they are
5943 Joined as required by ZSE however (otherwise they would be cryptographically unable to
5944 understand the information being sent to them by the Joined Devices).
5945 IHDs and other Type 2 Devices can only read application layer information from Devices to
5946 which they are Joined (either by requesting the information from the Device or by receiving
5947 information published by the Device). When a PPMID is joined to a GPF, the PPMID can only
5948 read information from the GPF to which it is Joined.
5949 When other types of Device are Joined (e.g. HCALCS, PPMID), they can also exchange
5950 Commands and Responses at the application layer. For example, an ESME that is Joined to
5951 an HCALCS can send a Command to the HCALCS to turn its switch on and the HCALCS can
5952 send a Response saying whether it has done that. A PPMID can send an ‘enable supply’
5953 Command to an ESME etc.
5954 The joining sequence – informative
5955 Statements in this Section 13.7.1.2 apply to an SAPC as if it were an ESME.
5956 There are three types of Join:
5957 Join Method B: this is a Join involving a Type 2 Device or a GPF;
5958 Join Method C: this is a Join between a GSME and a PPMID; and
5959 Join Method A: this is any Join which is not covered by Method B or C.
5960 Except for Method C, all Joins use the ZSE cryptography which requires exchange of
5961 messages between the two Devices to establish the shared secret that the two Devices will
5962 need to use. Method C uses the cryptography of Section 4 of this GBCS.
5963 Only certain combinations of Devices can be validly ‘Joined’. Table 13.7.1.2 summarises valid
5964 combinations:

5965  Table 13.7.1.2:  Permitted Joins
5966  A  Method A Join always involves an ESME and therefore any HAN exchanges required by a
5967  Method A Join shall always be instigated by the ESME involved.  In this context the ESME is
5968  referred to as the methodAInitiator, since it initiates Method A Joins.
5969  The additional step with a Method A Join is that the other Device must first be sent a Join
5970  Command detailing the ESME with which it is allowed to Join.  On receipt, the Device should
5971  add the ESME details to its Device Log and send a Response accordingly.  If, subsequently,
5972  the Device is asked to undertake key establishment, it must check that the requesting Device
5973  is in its Device Log.
5974  Only one Device in a Method B Join is remotely instructed.  Thus, the HAN exchanges
5975  required by a Method B Join shall always be instigated by the Device receiving such a
5976  Command.  From Table 13.7.1.2, this is always a GSME or ESME except where a GPF is to Join
5977  to a PPMID, IHD or CAD.  Thus, the sequence of a Method B Join is that the ESME / GSME /
5978  GPF:
5979  is sent a Join Command containing the Entity Identifier of the Device to which it is to Join
5980  and that other Device’s DeviceType;
5981  verifies the cryptographic protection on the Command and checks to make sure it is well
5982  formed and valid;
5983  updates its Device Log to include details of the new Device;
|     |     |     |     |     |     | Page 335  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --------- |

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
5984 for an ESME39, undertakes the key establishment process with the specified Device, as per
5985 the ZSE specification; and
5986 creates and sends a Response detailing the success or otherwise of its actions.
5987 A Method C join does not require exchange of Messages between the two Devices for the
5988 establishment of the shared secret. Thus the sequence of a Method C Join is that each of
5989 the GSME and PPMID:
5990 is sent a Join Command containing the Entity Identifier of the Device to which it is to Join,
5991 that other Device’s DeviceType and Key Agreement Certificate;
5992 verifies the cryptographic protection on the Command and does checks to make sure it is
5993 well formed and valid;
5994 updates its Device Log to include details of the new Device;
5995 checks there is a well-formed Device Certificate in the Command;
5996 optionally calculates the shared secret using the Device Certificate of the other Device
5997 (which is provided in the Command); and
5998 creates and sends a Response detailing the success or otherwise of its actions.
5999 The format of Message Payloads – informative
6000 In common with other GBCS Remote Messages related to the management of Security
6001 Credentials, the payloads of Commands and Responses defined in this Section 13.7.1.3 are
6002 specified using ASN.1, with DER encoding to be applied to Command and Response payloads.
6003 Device Requirements
6004 All Devices shall:
6005 support the ZSE Key Establishment Cluster as specified in Annex C of the ZSE cluster;
6006 support ‘Crypto Suite 2’ as defined in the ZSE specification; and
6007 use ‘Crypto Suite 2’ when undertaking any associated Key Establishment process.
6008 CHF, ESME, SAPC, HCALCS, PPMID and IHD shall support the mechanism at ZSE 5.4.7.4. A key
6009 that is provided to a pair of Devices by the CHF through that ZSE 5.4.7.4 mechanism shall, in
6010 this Section 13, be referred to as a ‘Partner Link Key’.
39 The shared secret between the Communications Hub and the Type 2 Device / GSME
established when the Device joined the HAN shall be used by the GPF to authenticate with
the Device.
Page 336

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
6011 An ESME shall be configured to be a ZSE ‘Router’, as defined in ZSE so that communications
6012 between the ESME and Devices Joined to the ESME, that are not operating on a Sub GHz
6013 Channel, are not reliant on availability of the Communications Hub.
6014 Where an SAPC is not operating on a Sub GHz Channel, the SAPC shall be configured to be a
6015 ZSE ‘Router’, as defined in ZSE so that communications between the SAPC and Devices
6016 Joined to the SAPC, that are not operating on a Sub GHz Channel, are not reliant on
6017 availability of the Communications Hub.
6018 Pursuant to the requirements in the SMETS and the CHTS requirement, Devices shall only
6019 communicate at an application layer with other Devices that are currently in their Device Log
6020 and are permitted by Device Based Access Controls (DBAC) as defined at Section 13.7.3.
6021 Such communications shall always be secured using the shared secrets established pursuant
6022 to Sections 13.7.4.
6023 Application layer communications within the scope of the DBAC requirement are HAN Only
6024 Messages, including provision of information to a PPMID or Type 2 Device. Note that HAN
6025 Only Messages between a PPMID and GSME have a structure that is specified in this GBCS in
6026 the corresponding Use Cases, and those relate only to Add Credit and Activate Emergency
6027 Credit Commands and the corresponding Responses.
6028 Access to the MeteringDeviceType attribute in the Metering Cluster shall not be within the
6029 scope of the DBAC requirements in Section 13.7.3, so as to facilitate use of the Partner Link
6030 Key mechanism as a pre-requisite to Joins involving an ESME or an SAPC.
6031 Each entry in a non CHF Device Log shall contain the Entity Identifier of the Authorised
6032 Device and its deviceType.
6033 The Entity Identifier of a Device with DeviceType of
6034 communicationsHubGasProxyFunction shall be the EUI 64-bit identifier of the
6035 ZigBee radio interface installed in the Communications Hub.
6036 Device Based Access Control
6037 In relation to information and functionality within SMETS, a Device shall, when it is a
6038 recipient of a Command or request for information from another Device on its SMHAN, only
6039 attempt to action that Command when:
6040 the sending Device’s Entity Identifier is in the recipient Device’s Device Log;
6041 the ZSE cryptographic protection on the Message is authenticated using the Shared Secret /
6042 Shared Secret Key established with the sending Device; and
6043 the Command or request for information is explicitly allowed by a cell in Tables 13.7.3a and
6044 13.7.3b, in terms of the DeviceType of the sending (client) and receiving (service) Device.

6079 Table 13.7.4.1: Join Device related Commands, Grouping and Message Categories
6080 Join Device Command and Response Processing
6081 Construction of Commands
6082 ‘Join Device’ Command Payloads shall be constructed as specified in Section 13.7.4.5.2 and
6083 Cryptographic Protection I and Cryptographic Protection II shall be applied as required for a
6084 Command of the relevant Message Category.
6085 For a Command (1) which complies with either Use Case ‘CS03A2 Method A Join (non
6086 Meter)’ or Use Case ‘CS03C Method C Join‘ and (2) where the Device to which it is addressed
6087 has a deviceType equal to type1PrepaymentInterfaceDevice, the Access
6088 Control Broker’s Digital Signing Private Key shall be used in generating the KRP Signature.
6089 Device processing of Commands and Response handling
6090 The Device receiving a ‘Join Device’ Command shall undertake processing steps in the
6091 sequence defined in this Section 13.7.4.2.2. Should a step after step 1 be unsuccessful, the
6092 Device shall create a Response according to the requirements of Section 13.7.4.5.2, apply
6093 the Response Cryptographic Protection required for a Response of the relevant Message
6094 Category, and send the Response and shall not undertake any further steps defined in this
6095 Section 13.7.4.2.2.
6096 In processing a ‘Join Device’ Command, the Device shall:
6097 1. undertake Command Authenticity and Integrity Verification as required for a Command
6098 of this Message Category, except that check 4 in Section 6.2.4.1.1 may be undertaken
6099 after the checks in Section 6.2.4.1.2. The Security Credentials used to verify
6100 Cryptographic Protection I shall be:
6101 those held in the {accessControlBroker, digitalSignature, management} Trust Anchor Cell, if
6102 deviceType equals type1PrepaymentInterfaceDevice; or
6103 those held in the {supplier, digitalSignature, management} Trust Anchor Cell, if deviceType
6104 does not equal type1PrepaymentInterfaceDevice;
Page 341

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
6105 2. verify the joinMethodAndRole as specified in Section 13.7.4.5.3;
6106 3. add the otherDeviceEntityIdentifier and otherDeviceType to its Device
6107 Log as specified in Section 13.7.4.5.4;
6108 4. if deviceType is eSME then undertake Key Establishment with the other Device as
6109 specified in Section 13.7.4.5.5;
6110 5. if joinMethodAndRole is methodC, and so the join is between a gSME and a
6111 type1PrepaymentInterfaceDevice, check that otherDeviceCertificate is
6112 present and validly structured. If the check succeeds the Device shall store, linked to
6113 this Device Log entry, details relating to otherDeviceCertificate, such that
6114 the Device is able to use subsequently the Shared Secret derived from
6115 otherDeviceCertificate and its own Private Key Agreement Key. If this check
6116 fails the Device shall set joinResponseCode to
6117 invalidOrMissingCertificate and processing shall be unsuccessful; and
6118 6. set joinResponseCode to success, create a Response according to the
6119 requirements of Section 13.4.7, apply the Response Cryptographic Protection required
6120 for a Response of the relevant Message Category, and send the Response.
6121 Response Processing
6122 Response Recipient Verification may be undertaken as specified in this GBCS for a Response
6123 of the relevant Message Category. The joinResponseCode field in the Response may be
6124 decoded according to the ASN.1 definitions at Section 13.7.4.5.1.
6125 ‘Unjoin Device’ Command and Response Processing
6126 Construction of Commands
6127 ‘Unjoin Device’ Command Payloads shall be constructed as specified in Section 13.7.4.6.2
6128 and Cryptographic Protection I and Cryptographic Protection II shall be applied as required
6129 for a Command of the relevant Message Category.
6130 For a Command where the Device to which it is addressed has a deviceType equal to
6131 type1PrepaymentInterfaceDevice, the Access Control Broker’s Digital Signing
6132 Private Key shall be used in generating the KRP Signature.
6133 Device processing of Commands and Response handling
6134 The Device receiving an ‘Unjoin Device’ Command shall undertake processing steps in the
6135 sequence defined in this Section 13.7.4.3.2.
6136 In processing an ‘Unjoin Device’ Command, the Device shall:
Page 342

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
6137 1. undertake Command Authenticity and Integrity Verification as required for a Command
6138 of this Message Category. The Security Credentials used to verify Cryptographic
6139 Protection I shall be:
6140 those held in the {accessControlBroker, digitalSignature, management} Trust Anchor Cell, if
6141 deviceType equals type1PrepaymentInterfaceDevice; or
6142 those held in the {supplier, digitalSignature, management} Trust Anchor Cell, if deviceType
6143 does not equal type1PrepaymentInterfaceDevice;
6144 2. set unjoinResponseCode to success;
6145 3. verify the otherDeviceEntityIdentifier matches an Entity Identifier currently recorded in
6146 its Device Log. If it does not then set unjoinResponseCode to
6147 otherDeviceNotInDeviceLog and process from step 5; otherwise process from step 4;
6148 4. delete all information from the entry in its Device Log that has the same Entity Identifier
6149 as otherDeviceEntityIdentifier along with all shared cryptographic material related to
6150 that entry. Additionally, If deviceType in that log entry is
6151 type1HANConnectedAuxiliaryLoadControlSwitch, the Device shall clear the association
6152 with the corresponding Auxiliary Controller [n], including updating the corresponding
6153 Auxiliary Controller [n] Type, with its SMETS meaning, to indicate that there is no
6154 associated Auxiliary Controller. If the deletion does not succeed, set
6155 unjoinResponseCode to otherFailure; and
6156 5. Create a Response according to the requirements of Section 13.7.4.6.2, apply the
6157 Response Cryptographic Protection required for a Response of the relevant Message
6158 Category, and send the Response.
6159 Response Processing
6160 Response Recipient Verification may be undertaken as specified in this GBCS for a Response
6161 of the relevant Message Category. The unjoinResponseCode field in the Response may
6162 be decoded according to the ASN.1 definitions at Section 13.7.4.6.1.
6163 ‘CS07 Read Device Join Details’ Command and Response Processing
6164 Construction of Commands
6165 ‘CS07 Read Device Join Details’ Command Payloads shall be constructed as specified in
6166 Section 13.7.4.7 and Cryptographic Protection II shall be applied as required for a Command
6167 of the SME.C.NC Message Category.

6274  Verification of joinMethodAndRole

6299 Adding the otherDeviceEntityIdentifier and otherDeviceType to the Device Log
6300 The Device shall undertake the following steps in the sequence specified:
Page 354

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
6301 1. if the otherDeviceEntityIdentifier matches an Entity Identifier currently recorded in its Device Log, then the Device shall compare
6302 deviceType in that log entry with otherDeviceType. If the Device types match then the addition is successful and processing within this
6303 Section 13.7.4.5.4 shall cease; otherwise the Device shall set joinResponseCode to incompatibleWithExistingEntry and processing within
6304 this Section 13.7.4.5.4 shall cease;
6305 2. the Device shall check if there is capacity for an additional entry in its Device Log, including confirmation that, where otherDeviceType is
6306 type1HANConnectedAuxiliaryLoadControlSwitch the Device does not currently have an Auxiliary Controller associated with all five of
6307 Auxiliary Controller [n]. If there is not, the Device shall set joinResponseCode to deviceLogFull and processing within this Section
6308 13.7.4.5.4 shall cease; and
6309 3. the Device shall attempt to create a new Device Log entry using otherDeviceEntityIdentifier and otherDeviceType. If that entry is not
6310 successfully created, the Device shall set joinResponseCode to writeFailure. If that entry is successfully created and otherDeviceType is
6311 type1HANConnectedAuxiliaryLoadControlSwitch, the Device shall associate one of its Auxiliary Controller [n] with this new HCALCS,
6312 including setting the corresponding Auxiliary Controller [n] Type, with its SMETS meaning, to indicate that this is an HCALCS whose Entity
6313 Identifier is otherDeviceEntityIdentifier.
6314 Undertaking Key Establishment with the other Device
6315 The Device shall undertake the following steps in the sequence specified:
6316 1. if the otherDeviceEntityIdentifier does not match an Entity Identifier for which the ESME has received a Partner Link Key,
6317 the Device shall set joinResponseCode to noPartnerLinkKeyReceived and processing within this Section 13.7.4.5.5 shall
6318 cease; and
6319 2. the ESME shall initiate, and attempt to complete, Key Establishment according to the ZSE requirements. The ESME shall wait a
6320 minimum of two seconds before timing out any key establishment operation. Should the first attempt to complete Key Establishment
6321 not succeed, the ESME shall wait 120 seconds before making a second attempt. If that second attempt fails, the ESME shall wait a
Page 355

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
6322 further 120 seconds before making a final attempt. If that final attempt does not succeed, the Device shall set joinResponseCode to the
6323 value specified by Table 13.7.4.5.5 or to noCBKEResponse if no response was received from the other Device.

6404 GCS59 / 62 GPF Device Log Backup and Restore
6405 Introduction to GPF Device Log Backup and Restore – informative
6406 The role of pair-wise authorisation – informative
6407 This Section 13.8 includes the Use Cases related to the backing up and restoring of the GPF's
6408 Device Log. This is to cater for situation where the existing Communications Hub fails and
6409 has to be replaced.
6410 In summary:
6411 a GPF sends an Alert whenever its Device Log changes (unless the change is as a result of a
6412 restore of the Device Log). That Alert contains the contents of the GPF's Device Log after the
6413 change has been made; and
6414 the Restore GPF Device Log Command shall contain the same structure of Device Log
6415 contents. If successful, the Command will place those contents in to the GPF's Device Log
6416 and will have triggered the processing required to authorise the specified Devices
6417 application layer interaction with the GPF, where required.
6418 The format of Message Payloads – informative
6419 In common with other GBCS Remote Messages related to the management of Security
6420 Credentials, the Payloads of Alerts, Commands and Responses defined in this Section 13.8
6421 are specified using ASN.1, with DER encoding to be applied to Command and Response
6422 payloads.
6423 Each entry in a GPF Device Log shall contain the Entity Identifier of the Authorised Device
6424 and its deviceType.
6425 GCS62 Backup GPF Device Log
6426 Description
6427 This Section 13.8.2 covers the creation, validation and processing of Alerts resulting from
6428 changes to the GPF Device Log. One such Alert shall be generated each time that the GPF
6429 Device Log changes, except where the change arises from a GPF Device Log Restore
6430 Command.

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
6455 The GPF receiving a GPF Device Log Restore Command shall undertake processing steps in the sequence defined in this Section 13.8.3.4. The
6456 Device shall undertake Command Authenticity and Integrity Verification as required for a Command of this Message Category, and then, if
6457 successful, for each DeviceLogEntry in deviceLogEntries, shall:
6458 1. set deviceLogEntry in the corresponding ResponseOutcome to the values of this DeviceLogEntry in deviceLogEntries;
6459 2. set joinResponseCode in the corresponding ResponseOutcome to success;
6460 3. if the deviceEntityIdentifier matches an Entity Identifier currently recorded in its Device Log, compare deviceType in that log entry with
6461 otherDeviceType. If the Device types match then the addition is successful and processing of this DeviceLogEntry shall cease; otherwise
6462 the Device shall set joinResponseCode to incompatibleWithExistingEntry and processing of this DeviceLogEntry shall cease;
6463 4. check if there is capacity for an additional entry in its Device Log. If there is not, the Device shall set joinResponseCode to deviceLogFull
6464 and processing of this DeviceLogEntry shall cease; and
6465 5. attempt to create a new Device Log entry using deviceEntityIdentifier and deviceType. If that entry is not successfully created, the Device
6466 shall set joinResponseCode to writeFailure and processing of this DeviceLogEntry shall cease.
6467 Once all DeviceLogEntry in deviceLogEntries have been processed, the GPF shall populate the Response Payload according to the requirements
6468 of Section 13.8.4.1 using the ResponseOutcomes produced by the processing in this Section 13.8.3.4, construct MAC Header, Grouping Header
6469 and apply the Response Cryptographic Protection required for a Response of the SME.C.NC Message Category, and send the Response.

6617 The Update Load Controller Security Credentials Command
6618 The Update Load Controller Security Credentials Command shall be the concatenation:
6619 MAC Header || Grouping Header ||
6620 @UpdateLoadControllerSecurityCredentials.CommandPayload || 0x40 || KRP Signature||
6621 ACB-SMD MAC
6622 with the requirements of Section 13.3.3.1, as to the components of that concatenation,
6623 applying as if @UpdateLoadControllerSecurityCredentials were @UpdateSecurityCredentials.
6624 The Update Load Controller Security Credentials Response
6625 An Update Security Credentials Response shall be the concatenation:
6626 Grouping Header || @ UpdateLoadControllerSecurityCredentials.ResponsePayload || 0x40
6627 || SMD Signature
6628 with the requirements of Section 13.3.3.2, as to the components of that concatenation,
6629 applying as if @UpdateLoadControllerSecurityCredentials were @UpdateSecurityCredentials.
6630 Future Dated Update Load Controller Security Credentials Alert
6631 A Future Dated Update Load Controller Security Credentials Alert shall be the concatenation:
6632 Grouping Header || @UpdateLoadControllerSecurityCredentials.AlertPayload || 0x40 ||
6633 SMD Signature
6634 where:
6635 @UpdateLoadControllerSecurityCredentials.AlertPayload shall be an octet string containing
6636 the DER encoding of the populated ASN.1 structure;
6637 Grouping Header in the Alert shall be constructed as specified in Section 7.2.7 with Business
6638 Target ID being the Entity Identifier specified in the corresponding Command’s Grouping
6639 Header;
6640 the Message Code being 0x0124; and
6641 SMD Signature shall be generated as specified in Section 6.3.5.
