6649 Updating Load Controller Security Credentials on a Device – Processing Steps
6650 This Section lays out the requirements for the construction, protection and Authentication
6651 of the Update Load Controller Security Credentials Command Payload, the processing
6652 required on the Device of the Command, the construction of the corresponding Response
6653 Payload and, where required, the Alert Payload.
6654 Command Payload construction
6655 The @ UpdateLoadControllerSecurityCredentials.CommandPayload shall have the structure
6656 defined in Section 13.10.5.11, and the Remote Party constructing the Command shall
6657 populate with values according to Table 13.3.4.1 as if:
6658 1. @UpdateLoadControllerSecurityCredentials were @UpdateSecurityCredentials;
6659 2. The allowed values for credentialsReplacementMode were either
6660 loadControllerByLoadController (10) or
6661 loadControllerBySupplier (11);
6662 3. Within authorisingRemotePartyTACellIdentifier the allowed values
6663 for trustAnchorCellRemotePartyRole were either supplier (2) or
6664 loadController (8);
6665 4. The otherRemotePartySeqNumberChanges sequence’s presence were
6666 Mandatory in all loadControllerBySupplier (11) Commands, since all
6667 such Commands effect a change of control;
6668 5. When present, the only allowed value for otherRemotePartyRole were
6669 loadController (8);
6670 6. Within targetTrustAnchorCell, the allowed value for
6671 trustAnchorCellRemotePartyRole were loadController (8); and
6672 7. executionDateTime were allowed to be present when
6673 credentialsReplacementMode were either
6674 loadControllerByLoadController (10) or
6675 loadControllerBySupplier (11).
6676 Command Authenticity and Integrity Verification
6677 The Device shall undertake processing according to the requirements of Section 13.10.5.1.
6678 Should any of the checks detailed in Section 13.10.5.1 fail then the Device shall:
Page 379

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
6679 generate an entry in the Security Log recording failed Authentication;
6680 discard the Command without execution and without sending a Response; and
6681 send an Alert notifying the failed Authentication, constructed as specified in Section 6.2.4.2
6682 of the GBCS, populated with the relevant Alert Code according to Section 16, to the Known
6683 Remote Party identified by the Trust Anchor Cell {supplier, digitalSignature, management}.
6684 Where all of the checks detailed in Section 13.10.5.1 succeed the Device shall process the
6685 Command and produce a Response.
6686 Command Processing
6687 Before undertaking any further processing, the Device shall update the Execution Counter
6688 for this type of Command to the value of authorisingRemotePartySeqNumber.
6689 If executionDateTime is present then the Device shall:
6690 record against the remotePartyRole (as specified in authorisingRemotePartyControl ),
6691 authorisingRemotePartyControl, replacements; and executionDateTime;
6692 construct a Response where executionOutcome is not present according to the
6693 requirements of Section 13.10.4.4; and
6694 at the date-time specified in executionDateTime, or immediately if the executionDateTime is
6695 in the past undertake the processing of Section 13.10.4.3.1 then construct an Alert according
6696 to the requirements of Section 13.10.4.5.
6697 If executionDateTime is not present then the Device shall:
6698 undertake the processing of Section 13.10.4.3.1; and
6699 construct a Response where executionOutcome is present according to the requirements of
6700 Section 13.10.4.4.
6701 replacements Processing
6702 For each of the targetTrustAnchorCell in replacements, the Device shall:
6703 record the entityIdentifier and subjectKeyIdentifier currently held in that
6704 targetTrustAnchorCell;
6705 attempt to replace the contents of that targetTrustAnchorCell using the corresponding
6706 certificate in TrustAnchorReplacement; and
6707 if the contents of the replacement are successfully applied, undertake the processing
6708 required by Section 13.10.5.10 in relation to the RemotePartyRole for that
6709 targetTrustAnchorCell.

6742 Preventing Replay of Commands
6743 The Protection Against Replay mechanisms for the Update Security Credentials Command
6744 shall be that specified in this Section 13.10.5.3 (which is different than that for other GBCS
6745 Commands).
6746 For each of RemotePartyRole from which the Device can receive a valid Updated Load
6747 Controller Security Credentials Command, the Device shall allocate storage for an Execution
6748 Counter which shall be capable of storing a 64 bit unsigned integer and which shall initially
6749 be set to the value zero at manufacture.
6750 Before executing any Update Security Credentials Command, a Device shall confirm that
6751 (authorisingRemotePartyTACellIdentifier is populated in the Command) and (the
6752 authorisingRemotePartySeqNumber is strictly numerically greater than the Execution
6753 Counter the Device has recorded for the RemotePartyRole identified in
6754 authorisingRemotePartyTACellIdentifier).
6755 Required Trust Anchor Cells by Device Type
6756 The Trust Anchor Cells specified in Section 4.3.2.5 for loadController are those
6757 required on each Device type and so are the only valid targetTrustAnchorCells.

6759 are valid for the type of Device it is, according to the requirements of Section 4.3.2.5. A

6781 Valid usage of Certificates against the targetTrustAnchorCells specified in the Command
6782 For each instance of the TrustAnchorReplacement structure in the Command, the keyUsage
6783 in replacementCertificate shall be equal to targetTrustAnchorCell.KeyUsage. Where this

6785 shall not be actioned by the Device.

6788 Verifying the Cryptographic Protections
6789 In verifying Cryptographic Protections:
6790 KRP Signature shall be verified using the public key identified in the Command; and
6791 ACB-SMD MAC shall be verified according to the requirements in Section 6.2.4.1.2.
6792 Verifying the authenticity of replacement certificates
6793 The Device shall first apply the requirements of Section 12.6 (Device processing of
6794 Certificates). If any of those checks fail, the Section 13.10.5.9 check fails.
6795 In relation to Certification Path Validation, the application of time based checks shall be
6796 determined as follows:
6797 if, in the Command, applyTimeBasedCPVChecks = disapply then time based checks shall NOT
6798 be applied by the Device; and
6799 otherwise time based checks shall be applied or not applied in line with the requirements of
6800 Section 4.3.2.8.
6801 The Device shall, for each replacementCertificate in replacements, undertake Certification
6802 Path Validation according to the requirements of Section 4.3.2.8.

6876 Table 14.1: Meanings of Defined Terms
6877 Maximum Credit Threshold and Maximum Meter Balance Threshold are represented using a
6878 value and associated scaler. The scaler determines the fractional part of the value, for
6879 example, to represent £123.25478 requiring a resolution of 5 decimal places would use a
6880 value of 12325478 and an associated scaler of -5 (i.e. multiply by 10-5). To interpret a value
6881 in whole Currency Units, the fractional part would be ignored, so for example, 12325478
6882 would become £123.
6883
6884 Description – informative
6885 This Section covers the application of a Prepayment Top Up, that has been purchased for a
6886 particular ESME or GSME, to that ESME or GSME.
6887 It covers four options:
6888 applying a Prepayment Top Up to an ESME without consumer intervention;
6889 applying a Prepayment Top Up to a GSME without consumer intervention;
6890 applying a Prepayment Top Up to an ESME or GSME with consumer entry of a numeric code
6891 on the ESME or GSME; and
6892 applying a Prepayment Top Up to an ESME or GSME with consumer entry of a numeric code
6893 on a PPMID.
6894 Some requirements are common to all four options. Accordingly, this Section 14 is split in to
6895 five subsections:
6896 an initial subsection covering requirements common to all four options; and
6897 four subsequent subsections covering one option in each subsection.
6898 By way of context:
6899 any Prepayment Top Up Message is a Remote Party Command in GBCS terms (because it is
6900 from a Remote Party to a GSME or ESME). The means of delivery (typing in on meter, typing
6901 in on PPMID, sending over WAN, etc.) does not affect this classification;
Page 389

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
6902 as a Remote Party Command, it must result in the GSME or ESME generating a Response
6903 back to the Remote Party who issued it (so the Supplier), unless there is an Authentication
6904 failure (in which case the Supplier has to be sent an Alert), as per the Technical
6905 Specifications;
6906 because the ranges are exclusive, the Originator Counter in Prepayment Top Up transactions
6907 cannot collide with the Originator Counter in any other transaction; and
6908 there is no requirement to include the Device’s ID explicitly in the locally entered transaction,
6909 so a PPMID joined to more than one Smart Meter will need to allow the Consumer to pick
6910 which Smart Meter the Prepayment Top Up is for.

6914 shall always be between 73 and 96, which shall be constructed and represented according to

6922 for the least significant bit.

6944 Checking the UTRN Counter against the UTRN Counter Cache
6945 The Device shall set the UTRN Counter to be the 32 most significant bits of the Originator
6946 Counter.
6947 The Device shall check that the UTRN Counter is strictly numerically greater than the
6948 numerically lowest value in the UTRN Counter Cache, and is not equal to any value in the
6949 UTRN Counter Cache.
6950 Updating the UTRN Counter Cache
6951 Where the Prepayment Top Up is successfully applied and prior to sending any Response,
6952 the Device shall add a new entry to the UTRN Counter Cache whose UTRN Counter value
6953 shall be set to the 32 most significant bits of Originator Counter.
6954 Validating the Maximum Credit Values
6955 Maximum Credit Threshold
6956 The Device shall ensure that the Prepayment Top Up’s value specified by PTUT Value Class
6957 and PTUT Value does not exceed the Device’s Maximum Credit Threshold parameter.
6958 Maximum Meter Balance Threshold
6959 The Device shall ensure that the Prepayment Top Up’s value specified by PTUT Value Class
6960 and PTUT Value when added to the Device’s Credit Balance does not exceed the Device’s
6961 Maximum Meter Balance Threshold parameter.
6962 Validating the PTUT Sub-Class
6963 The Device shall ensure that the value specified by PTUT Sub-Class is of value 0b0000.

7044 Verifying the UTRN Check Digit
7045 The Device:
7046 may validate the 20th digit (the UTRN Check Digit) as specified at Section 14.8 (Calculating
7047 and Verifying the UTRN Check Digit); and
7048 shall disregard the 20th decimal digit to determine PPTD prior to undertaking any
7049 subsequent checks.
7050 Using the PPTD to calculate the PTUT
7051 PTUT shall take the value of PPTD minus 7,394,156,990,786,306,048.
7052 The Device shall interpret the resulting unsigned integer according to Table 14.3.2.
7053 Verifying PTUT subclass category
7054 The Device shall carry out the checks specified in Section 14.3.9.
7055 Verifying against the maximum credit values
7056 The Device shall carry out the checks specified in Section 14.3.8.1 and Section 14.3.8.2.
7057 Deriving the Originator Counter45
7058 The Originator Counter shall be derived by:
7059 1. creating four 32 bit signed integer variables p, q, r and s;
7060 2. setting p = the numeric value of the 10 least significant bits of Highest UTRN Counter;
7061 3. setting q = (the numeric value Highest UTRN Counter) – p;
7062 4. setting r = the numeric value of PTUT Truncated Originator Counter;
7063 5. if r < (p – 29) then setting s = (r + 210) else if r > (p + 29) then setting s = (r – 210) else
7064 setting s = r;
7065 6. setting Originator Counter equal to ((q + s) * 232)
7066 Verifying the Originator Counter
45 This derivation places a practical limit on the maximum increment between issued
sequentially UTRN Counters. An increment of greater than (29 - 1) between a UTRN Counter
and the next one issued will cause this derivation to be inaccurate

7108 Command Construction by the PPMID
7109 Where the target Device is a GSME, the PPMID shall construct the Command according to

7111 Where the target Device is an ESME, the PPMID shall construct a ZSE Consumer Top Up

7113 In all cases:
7114 the value of the Top Up Code, with its ZSE meaning, shall be set to be a VisibleString whose
7115 value is the 20 digit UTRN; and
7116 the value of the Originating Device, with its ZSE meaning, shall be 0x02 (IHD).
7117 HAN Only Command Validation by the ESME / GSME
7118 If the ESME / GSME has no PPMID in its Device Log, the ESME / GSME shall apply the
7119 requirements of Section 6.2.4.2 to reflect the failed check, and undertake no additional
7120 processing.
7121 If the ESME / GSME has a PPMID in its Device Log:
7122 if the receiving Device is an ESME, the ESME shall use ZSE cryptographic processes to
7123 establish whether the Command was authentically issued by a PPMID that is in its Device
7124 Log; or
7125 if the receiving Device is a GSME, the GSME shall undertake Command Authenticity and
7126 Integrity Verification, as required for a Command of Message Category SME.C.PPMID-GSME
7127 to establish whether the Command was authentically issued by the PPMID that is in its
7128 Device Log. For clarity, the ‘PPMID entity ID’ and the ‘Meter entity ID’ from PCS01 and
7129 PCS02 Commands are the Business Originator ID and Business Target ID respectively used in
7130 the Section 6.2.4.1.1 checks.
7131 If the Command was not authentically issued by a PPMID within the Device Log, the ESME /
7132 GSME shall apply the requirements of Section 6.2.4.2 to reflect the failed check.
7133 If the Command was authentically issued by a PPMID within the Device Log, the ESME /
7134 GSME shall comply with the requirements of Section 14.6.4 (but excluding requirements in
7135 Sections 14.6.4.1.1, save that the ESME / GSME shall disregard the 20th digit before
7136 undertaking any further steps), and so process the contents of the Command accordingly.
7137 HAN Only Response Construction and Issue
7138 Where the ESME / GSME successfully creates a Remote Party Response to its Supplier, as per
7139 the requirements in Section 14.6.5, the ESME / GSME shall also:
Page 402

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
7140 where the Device is a GSME, construct the HAN Only Response according to the
7141 requirements of Use Case PCS01 and send it to the PPMID; or
7142 where the Device is an ESME, construct a ZSE Consumer Top Up Response command, and
7143 send it to the PPMID.
7144 In all cases the value of the Source of Top up, with its ZSE meaning, shall be 0x02 (IHD).
7145 Calculating and Verifying the UTRN Check Digit
7146 The UTRN Check Digit shall be calculated from the the PPTD by a process equivalent to the
7147 following (Verhoeff’s) Algorithm46:
7148 setting an interim digit (referred to as IntDig) to have a value of zero;
7149 setting an index (referred to as K) to have a value of four;
7150 repeating the following steps with another index (referred to as J) taking the nineteen values
7151 of the integers from 1 to 19 in succession;
7152 setting CurDig to the value of the Jth digit of the 19 decimal digits of the PPTD, where the
7153 first digit is the most significant (leftmost as written) and the nineteenth digit the least
7154 significant;
7155 setting a third index (referred to as L) to the value in Table 14.8a using K as the Row Index
7156 and CurDig as the Column Index;
7157 if the value of K is less than 7, setting K to the value of K+1, otherwise setting K to zero;
7158 setting IntDig to the value in Table 14.8b using IntDig as the Row Index and L as the Column
7159 Index;
7160 setting IntDig to the value in row 1 of Table 14.8c using the value of IntDig as the Column
7161 Index; and
7162 setting the UTRN Check Digit to the value of IntDig.
7163 The UTRN Check Digit may be verified by undertaking exactly the same calculation on the 19

7172 Message Codes
7173 Message Codes shall be 2 octets in length and shall take the values specified in the ‘Use Case

7177 Event / Alert Codes and related requirements
7178 Italicised terms in this Section 16 shall have their meaning in the ZCL / ZSE specifications.
7179 Introduction – informative
7180 This Section 16 sets out how Events and Alerts are handled. The Technical Specifications
7181 define when Events occur and whether these Events are logged (in an Event Log) and
7182 whether sent as an Alert via the HAN / WAN.
7183 Table 16.2 defines Event Codes for events defined in the Technical Specifications. It also
7184 indicates whether, as per the Technical Specifications, there is a corresponding Alert issued
7185 over the Device’s network interface (containing the relevant Event Code). It is important to
7186 note that not all Event Codes have a corresponding Alert. Where Alert Code is used
7187 elsewhere in this document, it equates to Event Code in Table 16.2.
7188 Alerts sent over the SMHAN are not subject to the same message categorisation as those
7189 sent over the WAN. An Alert sent over the SMHAN is a native ZSE message.
7190 Types of Alert
7191 There are two Alert types. All have the same Grouping Header but different payloads as set
7192 out below:
7193 Alert type 1 - Payload comprises Alert Code and Timestamp only (two sub-types: DLMS and
7194 ZigBee). These are labelled ‘Y(1)’ in the ‘Alert WAN (Alert type)’ column in Table 16.2; and
7195 Alert type 2 - Payload comprises Alert Code, Timestamp and Use Case specific data as
7196 defined in Table 16.2 or main body of document (three sub-types: ASN.1, DLMS and ZigBee).
7197 These are labelled ‘Y(2)’ in the ‘Alert WAN (Alert type)’ column in Table 16.2.
Page 405

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
7198 Table 16.2 sets out the Alert type for each Alert Code. Examples of Use Case specific data
7199 include Billing Data Logs and content relating to future dated Commands (e.g. Message ID).
7200 Table 16.2 sets out whether Alerts are mandated, mandatory conditional or non-mandated:
7201 Mandated - Alerts that Devices of the applicable Device Type must support;
7202 Mandated conditional – Devices of the applicable Device Type must support at least one
7203 from the specified group (e.g. there are seven Alerts in ‘mandated – conditional group 1’,
7204 Devices must support at least one of these seven); and
7205 Non-mandatory – no requirement for Devices to support, but where implemented Alert
7206 Codes shall have the meaning shown in Table 16.2.
7207 An SAPC shall support the Alerts, and support corresponding logging requirements, for rows
7208 in Table 16.2 marked ‘mandatory’ in the column titled ‘SAPC support’. For clarity, ‘ECS100
7209 Command not supported by Device’ is marked as ‘mandatory’ and must be supported by an
7210 SAPC unless the SAPC supports all Use Cases required of an ESME which is a Single Element
7211 Electricity Metering Equipment, with its SMETS meaning.
7212 An SAPC, where it has a Boost Function, with its SMETS meaning, shall support the Alerts,
7213 and support corresponding logging requirements, for rows in Table 16.2 marked ‘mandatory
7214 where the SAPC has a Boost Function, with its SMETS meaning’ in the column titled ‘SAPC
7215 support’.
7216 An SAPC shall support, for each group, at least one of the Alerts, and support corresponding
7217 logging requirements, for rows in Table 16.2 marked ‘mandatory – conditional group N’ in
7218 the ‘SAPC support’ column, where ‘N’ is a number.
7219 An SAPC shall additionally support the Alerts, and corresponding logging requirements, for
7220 rows in Table 16.2 marked ‘optional’ in the ‘SAPC support’ column, where the SAPC supports
7221 the corresponding SMETS functionality.

7239 Event Logs

7241 16.2 to log entries into Event Logs only applies to GSME, SAPC, ESME, CHF and GPF as

7246 functionality); and
7247 Auxiliary Controller Event Log (SAPC and ESME).
7248 Use Cases to read logs (all) and clear logs (event logs only) are detailed in the Mapping Table.
7249 Requirements
7250 Event / Alert codes shall be 2 octets in length and shall take the values specified in Table 16.2.
7251 As per the Technical Specifications, all Alerts, Event Log entries, Security Log entries, Power
7252 Event Log entries and Auxiliary Controller Event Log entries shall contain a UTC date time
7253 stamp, in addition to the Event / Alert code. For Event / Alert Codes beginning 0x80 or 0x81
7254 in Table 16.2 which relate to a GSME or ESME, the requirements in Table 16.2 in relation to:
7255 sending Alerts;
7256 notifying events to other Devices to which it is connected by means of a Communications
7257 Link; and
7258 logging events in the Event Log or Power Event Log,

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
7259 shall be those configured in ESME, SAPC and GSME prior to installation.
7260 In relation to Event / Alert Codes 0x8161 and 0x8162 and the notification of those events to
7261 other Devices to which the Device is connected by means of a Communication Link, the
7262 Device shall be configured prior to installation so as to not send such notifications unless:
7263 the Device is an ESME which includes an APC; or
7264 the Device is an SAPC which includes a User Interface and that User Interface provides
7265 access to User Interface Commands detailed in Table 16.4;
7266 in which cases:
7267 the Device shall be configured prior to installation so as to send such notifications; and
7268 when sending such notifications, the Device shall, in relation to any ZigBee Publish Event
7269 command used to send such a notification:
7270 populate the Event Data parameter with the value 0x02 || (Table 16.4 ‘User
7271 Interface Command Code’ corresponding to the Command invoked); and
7272 populate the Event ID parameter with either 0x8161 or 0x8162 to reflect the
7273 Outcome of that Command.
7274 For clarity, the requirement to populate the Event Data parameter applies only to ESME with
7275 APC and SAPC with a User Interface. Other Devices, if configured after installation to notify
7276 events Event / Alert Codes 0x8161 and 0x8162, would not be required to populate that field
7277 with the Table 16.4 value, and so that value may not be present. Alternatively, for these
7278 other Devices a value may be present but may not follow the requirements of this Section
7279 16.4.
7280 Prior to installation, all such Event / Alert Codes shall be configured not to sound an Alarm.
7281 For clarity, Event / Alert Codes beginning 0x8F and any applying on Devices other than ESME
7282 / GSME / SAPC are not configurable and Table 16.2 specifies the fixed settings. Once
7283 installed, the configurations relating to sending Alerts, notifying other Devices, logging and
7284 sounding Alarms may be modified using the event and Alert configuration Use Cases.
7285 GSME shall reject any ZSE SetEventConfiguration command containing an Event ID in the
7286 Event Configuration Payload with 0x8F in the most significant octet, to ensure Critical Alerts
7287 are always configured on. For clarity, the ESME Alert Configuration Use Cases, which may
7288 also be supported by SAPC, do not allow for Alert Codes starting 0x8F.
7289 SAPC is not required to support the Event / Alert configuration Use Cases. Where SAPC does
7290 not support such Use Cases, the settings required by Table 16.2 shall remain unchanged,
7291 including for any Event / Alert Codes beginning 0x80 or 0x81.

7309 to the WAN Provider if deviceType = 0x02 (CHF); or
7310 to the Supplier for all other deviceType values.

7350 Remote Party Usage Rights
7351 Remote Party Access Rights to Attributes and Methods
7352 Access rights to attributes and methods shall be enforced by the Device as per the
7353 requirements in the ‘SMETS required objects’ tab in the Mapping Table. ‘R’ shall mean that
7354 the Remote Party Role shall have read access to the attribute. ‘W’ shall mean that the
7355 Remote Party Role shall have write access to the attribute. ‘A’ shall mean that the Remote
7356 Party Role shall be able to invoke the method. There shall be no other access to these
7357 attributes and methods allowed by the Device.
7358 Encryption of attributes whenever transiting the HAN Interface shall be enforced by the
7359 Device as per the requirements in the ‘SMETS required objects’ tab in the Mapping Table. ‘Y’
7360 in the column headed ‘Encrypted’ shall mean that the Encryption shall always be applied to
7361 the corresponding attribute as it crosses the HAN Interface.
7362 Remote Party Usage Rights to Use Cases
7363 Access rights to Use Cases shall be enforced by the Device as per the requirements in the
7364 Use Case Access Permissions table in each Use Case (see Table 19.3). A Remote Party Role in
7365 that table shall have access to the Use Case. There shall be no other access allowed by the
7366 Device. Remote Party roles align to the Trust Anchor Cells in Section 4.3.2.5. The Access
7367 Control Broker controls access for Unknown Remote Parties.

7376 ZSE Load Control Event command
7377 The ZSE Load Control Event command shall be sent by an ESME:
7378 following successful authentication of a Command with Message Code 0x011E (so ‘ECS47a
7379 Set Auxiliary Controller [n] State’), where that command requires an HCALCS to change its
7380 state;
7381 to control an HCALCS according to the Auxiliary Controller Calendar; or
Page 412

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
7382 as required by Section 18.1.1.3.
7383 In executing this command, the ESME shall send the ZCL Load Control Event command to the
7384 HCALCS identified in that Command / in that Get Scheduled Events command / in that entry
7385 of the Auxiliary Controller Calendar (as determined by the requirements of Section 7.3.6.1)
7386 with:
7387 the values of each field populated in the ZCL Load Control Event command as specified in
7388 Table 18.1.1.1;
7389 the ‘Duration in Minutes’ field set according to the respective triggers above calculated as
7390 per SMETS;
7391 the ‘Duty Cycle’ field set to 0x00 or to 0x64, determined according to the requirements of
7392 Section 7.3.6.1.
7393 The recipient HCALCS shall interpret the value in Duty Cycle accordingly.
7394 Whenever it sends a Load Control Event command, the ESME shall add an entry to the
7395 Auxiliary Controller Event Log where:
7396 hanCommandID is set to the value of the Issuer Event ID in the command;
7397 outcome is set to 0x00 (‘Outcome not known’); and
7398 switchNumberAndAction is set to the concatenation 0x1‘n’ (where ‘n’ is the value of
7399 Auxiliary Controller [n] for the HCALCS in question) || Duty Cycle in the command.
7400 On successful authentication of such a ZCL command, the recipient HCALCS shall respond
7401 with a Report Event Status ZCL command populated as per Table 18.1.1.4, with Event Status
7402 set to:
7403 0x02 (‘Event started’), if the command was successfully executed; or
7404 0xFE (‘Load Control Event command Rejected’), if the command was not successfully
7405 executed.
7406 Whenever it receives a Report Event Status command with an Event Status of either 0x02 or
7407 0xFE, the ESME shall add an entry to the Auxiliary Controller Event Log where:
7408 hanCommandID is set to the value of the Issuer Event ID in the command;
7409 outcome is set to:
7410 1. 0x01 (‘Success’) if Event Status is 0x02 (‘Event started’) in the
7411 command; or

7433 Table 18.1.1.4: ZSE Report Event Status command
7434 Message Template for ZSE commands between SAPC / ESME with APC and PPMID / Type 2
7435 Device
7436 ZSE Load Control Event command
7437 In this section:
7438 Source Device shall mean either (1) an ESME with at least one APC or (2) an SAPC; and
7439 Requesting Device shall mean a Device which is (1) in the Source Device’s Device Log and (2)
7440 is a Type 2 Device or a PPMID, according to the Source Device’s Device Log.
7441 Where the Source Device has received a ZDO Bind Request in relation to the Demand
7442 Response and Load Control Cluster from a Requesting Device (regardless of whether the
7443 Source Device supports binding with its ZigBee meaning), the Source Device shall:
7444 whenever, in relation to any of its Auxiliary Controller [n], the Source Device has changed the
7445 current output level; or
7446 when its Auxiliary Controller [n] is an APC, the Source Device has changed the current input
7447 level, or input limit level or output limit level;
7448 Send a ZSE Load Control Event command to the Requesting Device, populated as specified in
7449 Table 18.1.2.1 for the Auxiliary Controller [n] whose level has changed. If:
7450 the Load Control Event Command issued has a value of 1440 minutes for the ‘Duration In
7451 Minutes’ parameter; and
7452 1440 minutes then elapse without the Source Device sending a subsequent Load Control
7453 Event Command to the Requesting Device in relation to Auxiliary Controller [n];
7454 then the Source Device shall send a Load Control Event Command to the Requesting Device
7455 in relation to Auxiliary Controller [n]’s now current levels.
7456 For clarity:
7457 the above requirements for the Service Device pushing ZSE Load Control Event commands
7458 are additional to any other ZigBee or GBCS requirements to push such commands;
7459 the Requesting Device shall not be required to undertake any ZigBee specified client
7460 processing specific to the Load Control Event Command; and
7461 the Requesting Device shall not respond to the Load Control Event with a Report Event
7462 Status Command (the use of a reserved bit in the Device Class bitmap of the Load Control
7463 Event ensures that this behaviour aligns with the ZSE requirements).
Page 417

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
7464 Where the Source Device receives an authenticated Get Scheduled Events Command from a
7465 Requesting Device (so a Device which is not an HCALCS according to the Source Device’s
7466 Device Log), the Source Device shall, for each of Auxiliary Controller [n] (where n = 1 to 5)
7467 which has an associated ALCS or APC:
7468 where Auxiliary Controller [n] is an ALCS, send a ZSE Load Control Event command to the
7469 Requesting Device, populated as specified in Table 18.1.2.1 detailing the current state;
7470 where Auxiliary Controller [n] is an APC, send two ZSE Load Control Event commands to the
7471 Requesting Device, populated as specified in Table 18.1.2.1, one detailing the current input
7472 levels and the other detailing the current output levels; and
7473 where Auxiliary Controller [n] is an APC or an ALCS, send, for each of the next 25 state
7474 changes which are required by the currently configured Auxiliary Controller Calendar and
7475 which relate to Auxiliary Controller [n], a ZSE Load Control Event command to the
7476 Requesting Device, populated as specified in Table 18.1.2.1. Where there are fewer than 25
7477 such state changes, the Source Device shall send such lower number of commands as is
7478 required to detail all such state changes, as are specified by the configured Auxiliary
7479 Controller Calendar.
7480 For clarity, this means that 1 authenticated Get Scheduled Events Command from a
7481 Requesting Device can result in a maximum of 135 ZSE Load Control Event commands from
7482 the Source Device (specifically in the case where the Source Device has five APCs installed =
7483 5 x (2 (current states) + 25 (future states)).
7484 The Source Device shall not apply any ZSE specified requirements specific to the processing
7485 of Get Scheduled Events Commands, and so shall discard the values of any parameters in the
7486 ZCL payload of such Commands.

7499 Compact array encoding
7500 The Blue Book definition of attribute 2 of Profile Generic objects may be interpreted as
7501 requiring ‘entry’ to be a structure containing a single choice from the DLMS data types. The
7502 GBCS interprets it as meaning that ‘entry’ is a structure that can contain multiple choices of
7503 DLMS data types. These choices vary between instances of Profile Generic object. To
7504 identify these different structures, the naming convention ‘entry_nameOfStructure’ is used.
7505 The GBCS uses the compact-array data type in attribute 2 of Profile Generic objects. Table
7506 18.2.1.1 details the derivation of the contents-description element within the compact-array
7507 structure for the structures used in the Profile Generic objects required by this GBCS. These
7508 encodings are reflected in the DLMS COSEM Message Templates.

7529  0x02030906 || credit object OBIS code || 0x0906 || charge object OBIS code || 0x0403 || collection bit string || 0b00000
7530  The meaning of each credit_charge_configuration_element is that this charge can be collected from this credit object, except in possible meter
7531  states specified by the collection_configuration bit string.
7532  On an ESME, there shall be three class 112 Credit objects, as shown in Table 18.2.1.3b.  Two are not relevant in Credit Mode.
| SMET Reference          | OBIS Code        | OBIS Code       | Payment Mode           |     |
| ----------------------- | ---------------- | --------------- | ---------------------- | --- |
| Component               | (decimal)        | (hexadecimal)   |                        |     |
| MeterBalance            | 0-0:19.10.0.255  | 0x0000130A00FF  | Prepayment and Credit  |     |
| AccumulatedDebt         | 0-0:19.10.2.255  | 0x0000130A02FF  | Prepayment             |     |
| EmergencyCreditBalance  | 0-0:19.10.1.255  | 0x0000130A01FF  | Prepayment             |     |
7533  Table 18.2.1.3b:  Class 112 Credit objects

7535  Credit Mode.

7537  As defined in the Blue Book, the collection_configuration bit string determines whether a charge is collected from a credit dependent on ESME
7538  state.
7539  Bit 1 affects charging in load limiting periods. There is no such requirement in SMETS, so this value is always 0b1 (charges are applied in load
7540  limiting periods).
7541  In Credit Mode, collection continues in all states, so the value of all three bits is always 0b1.
7542  In Prepayment Mode, collection_configuration is set according to Suspend Debt Disabled (affects Bit 0) values, and the pairing of charge and
7543  credit object.
7544  Suspend Debt Emergency being True means that DebtRecoveryRates[1..2] and StandingCharge are collected from AccumulatedDebt rather
7545  than EmergencyCreditBalance, when Emergency Credit is in use, so Suspend Debt Emergency is specified by way of pairing charge and credit
7546  objects accordingly.  Note that Bit 2 of collection_configuration shall always be fixed at 0b1.
7547  Suspend Debt Disabled being True means that DebtRecoveryRates[1..2] are no longer collected when the supply is disabled due to lack of
7548  credit.
7549  Table 18.2.1.3d sets out the credit_charge_configuration_element array entries in Credit Mode.

7575  Where the periodicity is quarterly or longer, this Section sets out how the components of the Billing Calendar start date-time and periodicity
7576  shall be encoded in attribute 4 (execution_time) of the DLMS COSEM class 22 (OBIS 0-0:15.0.0.255 in Use Case ECS30a).
7577  If the required periodicity is quarterly (so once every three months), the execution_time shall be encoded as per Table 18.2.1.5a.
7578  If the required periodicity is six monthly, the execution_time shall be encoded as per Table 18.2.1.5b.
7579  If the required periodicity is yearly, the execution_time shall be encoded as per Table 18.2.1.5c.
7580  Note that month values are to be calculated using modulo twelve addition. For example, if quarterly billing is required and the start date-time
7581  is in October (so month 10), the value of months in the following three quarters is calculated by adding three modulo 12, so giving 1 (January),
7582  4 (April) and 7 (July).

7590  Encoding to turn daily Block Counter resetting on and off
7591  This Section sets out how attribute 4 (execution_time) of the DLMS COSEM class 22 object (OBIS 0-0:15.1.0.255 in Use Case ECS48) is to be set,
7592  so as to either turn on or off daily resetting of Block Counters.
7593  If daily resetting of Block Counters is required, the execution_time shall be encoded as per Table 18.2.1.6a.

7604 Execution Counters. In business terms, an example of this would be at Change of Supplier.

7624  of such attributes.

7684 Pre-conditions
7685 Pre-conditions represent conditions for which Device logic is required to ensure correct
7686 operation of commands contained within a message, on the Device. Exception conditions
7687 (such as failures) that are managed by the Protocol are not captured as Pre-conditions.
7688 Manufacturers of Devices must only enforce Pre-conditions that are stated in the Use Cases.
7689 Note that the use of Pre-conditions is minimised in favour of controls being implemented on
7690 Service User systems.
7691 Actions
7692 Actions stipulate additional Device actions that must be performed together with successful
7693 execution of the Use Case.
7694 Use Case-specific content
7695 Each Use Case is given a unique reference and a title.

7697 Table 19.2.1 sets out the Use Case specific attributes and methods and the DLMS specific
7698 mapping.
7699 Within any DLMS COSEM Payload, cosem-attribute-descriptors and cosem-method-
7700 descriptors, and associated fields, shall be ordered based on the contents of columns in the
7701 Mapping Table. The sort order, described by columns headings in the Mapping Table, shall
7702 be:
7703 first by DLMS Sequence;
7704 then by DLMS: Class;
7705 then by OBIS Code;
7706 then by Attribute (A) / Method (M); and
7707 then by Attribute / Method Number.
7708 The sort order shall be ascending in all cases.
7709 For structures, the sequence of elements within a structure shall be as defined in the Blue
7710 Book, where it is defined in the Blue Book, or as per the Mapping Table, where it is not
7711 defined in the Blue Book.
7712 For clarity, the SMETS / CHTS table in each Use Case is sorted in this same order.

7743 Glossary
7744 ||
7745 X || Y shall mean the concatenation of the two octet strings X and Y.
7746 Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1)
7747 ASN.1 is a standard notation for the definition of data types and values. A data type (or type
7748 for short) is a category of information (for example, numeric, textual, still image or video
7749 information). A data value (or value for short) is an instance of such a type. ASN.1 defines
7750 several basic types and their corresponding values, and rules for combining them into more
7751 complex types and values. In some protocol architectures, each message is specified as the
7752 binary value of a sequence of octets. However, standards-writers need to define quite
7753 complex data types to carry their messages, without concern for their binary representation.
7754 In order to specify these data types, they require a notation that does not necessarily
7755 determine the representation of each value. ASN.1 is such a notation.
7756 Access Control Broker (ACB)
7757 In the context of a specific Device, the Known Remote Party whose Security Credentials are
7758 stored in the {accessControlBroker, digitalSignature, management} Trust Anchor Cell where
7759 present, and stored in the {accessControlBroker, keyAgreement, management} Trust Anchor
7760 Cell otherwise.
7761 The ACB applies Cryptographic Protections to all Commands addressed to the Device in
7762 question, except potentially for certain recovery scenarios catered for by the Security
7763 Credentials Commands.
7764 Access Control Broker to Device MAC (ACB-SMD MAC)
7765 A MAC generated by the Access Control Broker in relation to a Command which can only be
7766 verified by the Device which is the target of the Command.

8408 Annex 4 – Use of ZigBee in GBCS – informative
8409 Purpose
8410 This annex briefly summarises where the GBCS:
8411 requires the use of ZigBee, specifically where it uses parts of the ZigBee specifications, or
8412 takes an approach which aligns to the ZigBee specifications; and
8413 does not allow the use of ZigBee / requires its use to be modified, specifically where it:
8414 mandates a solution that is not ZigBee derived but where there is ZigBee equivalent in the
8415 specifications;
8416 specifies an approach that is derived from ZigBee but the approach is not part of the ZigBee
8417 specifications; and
8418 specifies an approach that uses parts of the ZigBee but varies from it on specific points.
8419 The document is based on the content of ZigBee specifications referenced in the GBCS.
8420 GBCS requirements to use ZigBee
8421 For all Smart Metering Equipment, the GBCS requires the implementation of functionality
8422 equivalent to a subset of the ZigBee standards, including all mandatory components
8423 required to achieve ZSE certification.
8424 GBCS and the ZigBee standards specify all items that need to be certified.
8425 GBCS requirements not to use ZigBee / vary from it
8426 This Section summarises areas where GBCS requires that parts of the ZigBee standards are
8427 not used or used in a different way. It is an informative summary. The normative
8428 requirements are as stated in the normative Sections of this document.
Page 527

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
8429 For some communications between Devices, GBCS requires a solution other than solely
8430 ZigBee. For example, Commands from a PPMID to a GSME (and the corresponding
8431 Responses) are GBCS specified and carried in ZSE TransferData commands.
8432 GBCS requires certain ZigBee features to have a GB-specific interpretation. For example,
8433 Section 10.4.2.11 specifies how the ZSE AccumulatedDebt attribute shall be populated by
8434 the GSME and interpreted by all other devices.
8435 GBCS requires specific population of certain ZigBee commands for GB usage. For example,
8436 Section 10.4.2.11 specifies how the ZSE Get Event Log and Clear Event Log commands can be
8437 used to access GSME Proxy Log copies of the GSME Event or Security Log on the GPF.
8438 GBCS requires a different interpretation of certain ZigBee parameters to support GB usage.
8439 For example, Section 10.4.2.11 specifies that when using the ZSE GetSampledData and
8440 GetSampledDataResponse commands, a SampleRequestInterval field shall contain 0xFFFF
8441 whenever the SampleID field is 0x0001. GBCS specifies that a SampleID of 0x0001
8442 corresponds to the Daily Consumption Log, and SMETS specifies that this log contains
8443 reading data taken at midnight UTC, so once every 24 hours. This is a longer period than can
8444 be specified in the SampleRequestInterval, given that parameter’s size and hence the
8445 deviation from the standard.
8446 GBCS lays out specific requirements regarding the use of Inter-PAN communications
8447 between a Communications Hub and an HHT. These are stated in Section 10.
8448 GBCS bars or modifies some internal Device behaviour that is specified in ZigBee standards,
8449 for example:
8450 The ZSE capability for the OTA Client to self-activate any Firmware is not allowed, as stated in
8451 Section 11.2.1.
8452 The ZSE constraint requiring Trust Center involvement in CBKE shall not be applied, as stated
8453 in Section 13.7.2.
8454 GBCS does not require ZSE certification either for non-standard ZSE features or for non-ZSE
8455 features in GBCS.
8456 Annex 5 – Use of DLMS COSEM in GBCS – informative
8457 Statements in the Section regarding an ESME apply to an SAPC as if it were an ESME, where
8458 the SAPC supports the functionality to which the statement relates.
8459 Statements that do not apply to an ESME also do not apply to an SAPC.
8460 Purpose
8461 This annex briefly summarises where the GBCS:

8462 requires the use of DLMS COSEM: specifically where it uses parts of the DLMS COSEM
8463 specification, or takes an approach which aligns to the DLMS COSEM specification; and
8464 does not allow the use of DLMS COSEM / requires its use to be modified: specifically where
8465 it:
8466 Mandates a solution that is not DLMS COSEM derived but where there are DLMS COSEM
8467 equivalents;
8468 Specifies an approach that is derived from DLMS COSEM but the approach is not part of the
8469 DLMS COSEM specification; or
8470 Specifies an approach that uses parts of the DLMS COSEM but varies from it on specific
8471 points.
8472 GBCS requirements to use DLMS COSEM
8473 For ESME and CHF, the GBCS requires the implementation of functionality equivalent to a
8474 subset of the Blue Book Classes. It does not require functionality equivalent to other Blue
8475 Book classes not identified in the GBCS.
8476 For all Devices, GBCS requires a set of cryptographic primitives that align to DLMS Security
8477 Suite 1, and so all Devices will need functionality which is in line with the cryptography
8478 related parts of the Green Book (for both GBCS and DLMS COSEM, these requirements are
8479 NIST derived).
8480 GBCS requires that all Devices use X.509 Certificates and Certification Requests with a
8481 number of optional elements being used / barred. These requirements align with the Green
8482 Book requirements (which are X.509 derived).
8483 For ESME and CHF, the GBCS requires functionality equivalent to Green Book access and
8484 data notification services.
8485 For all Devices, the GBCS requires functionality equivalent to the Green Book’s general
8486 ciphering and general signing services.
8487 For all Devices, the GBCS requires functionality equivalent to the Green Book’s authenticated
8488 encryption and decryption.
8489 For all Devices, the GBCS requires corresponding alignment with DLMS COSEM’s ASN.1
8490 schema and its A-XDR encoding.
8491 GBCS requirements not to use DLMS COSEM / vary from it
8492 Mandates a solution that is not DLMS COSEM derived but where there are DLMS COSEM
8493 equivalent in the specification
Page 529

SEC Schedule 8 – GBCS v4.4
8494 For Devices other than ESME and CHF, the GBCS requires functionality equivalent to DLMS
8495 COSEM classes but does not use DLMS COSEM classes (rather GBZ / ASN.1 is used).
8496 For Devices other than ESME and CHF, the GBCS requires support for equivalents of the
8497 Green Book’s access and data notification services, but uses GBZ or ASN.1 specific structures.
8498 For all Devices, the GBCS requires that the management of X.509 certificates and Device’s
8499 key pairs is undertaken using ASN.1 messages derived from the IETF’s TAMP RFCs.
8500 Over the HAN, the GBCS mandates, for all Devices, the use of ZigBee for the communication
8501 layers below the DLMS/COSEM Application Layer and so does not allow the use of the
8502 equivalent Green Book communication profiles. (WAN transport is outside GBCS scope).
8503 For ESME and GSME, distribution of firmware is through the ZSE OTA mechanism.
8504 Specifies an approach that is derived from DLMS COSEM but the approach is not part of the
8505 specification
8506 GBCS specifies the use of a Class 9000 object, not specified in the Blue Book.
8507 For large Remote Party Messages, the GBCS uses DLMS type structures but in a way not
8508 specified in the DLMS COSEM specification.
8509 Messages using pairwise key agreement between GSME and PPMID uses a structure similar
8510 to DLMS COSEM’s message structure, but that structure is not part of the DLMS COSEM
8511 specification.
8512 Specifies an approach that uses parts of the DLMS COSEM but varies from it on specific
8513 points
8514 For all bar Type 2 Devices, the DLMS general-signing structure is used in all Remote Party
8515 Messages but the signature field is not populated in Messages that do not require a
8516 signature (i.e. those that are not critical).
8517 For all bar Type 2 Devices, the GBCS uses the general-ciphering structure for Remote Party
8518 Messages that require a MAC. The GBCS leaves most values empty in the header part of the
8519 structure (these values are either in the general-signing structure or are already known to
8520 the meter). Correspondingly, the values used in the OtherInput field of the KDF at section
8521 9.2.3.4.6.5 of the Green Book are those taken from the general-signing structure, rather
8522 than the corresponding fields in the general-ciphering structure.
8523 For ESME and GSME, the GBCS specifies particular, additional interpretation of parameters
8524 within the DLMS COSEM Class 8 object (Clock).

8525  Annex 6 – Deducing the UTRN Counter from the Truncated UTRN Counter – informative
8526  This annex provides a worked example of the calculation described in Section 14.6.4.1.5.  The calculation uses the 10-bit Truncated UTRN
8527  Counter received with the Prepayment Top Up command is received via Consumer Entry to the Device, either directly or via a PPMID.  The
8528  calculation uses the highest UTRN Counter value held in the Device’s UTRN Counter cache, and a window of 512 either side of this value in
8529  making the deduction.
8530  In this case, the UTRN Counter being entered into the Device is 5 greater than the highest thus far received by the Device.
